Īśopaniṣad 1.alt: A single continuous landscape of river, trees, grazing deer, a tiny village and distant mountains, all gently permeated by the same subtle golden daylight. A modest person receives a small bowl of fruit with open hands while leaving the abundance of the living world undisturbed. Evoke divine pervasion, enjoyment with relinquishment, and freedom from coveting; no anthropomorphic deity.

Īśopaniṣad 2.alt: A humble person working attentively in a small field and watering a sapling at dawn, with a mature tree nearby suggesting a long life of purposeful action. Open, unpossessive hands and quiet sustained work, no chains or trophies. Evoke acting throughout a hundred-year life without being bound by action.

Īśopaniṣad 3.alt: A solitary tiny traveler at the threshold of a sunless mist-covered valley, their face turned away from a small warm light behind them. Atmospheric indigo-gray darkness veils the landscape without horror. Symbolic spiritual blindness and forgetting the Self; no injury, death, corpse, self-harm, demons or punishment imagery.

Īśopaniṣad 4.alt: A still, clear pool at the center of a windswept landscape. Rushing clouds, moving grasses and birds suggest the swiftness of thought, while a single unwavering reflection of soft light remains still. Wind moves across water. Interpret the unmoving Self, swifter than thought, and Matarishvan sustaining activity; no human embodiment of the Self.

Īśopaniṣad 5.alt: A dewdrop on a leaf in the foreground reflecting the same far mountain and sky that extend behind it. A nearby quiet pond and distant moving clouds merge into one continuous atmosphere. Evoke the near and far, moving and unmoving, within and beyond; no separate collage panels.

Īśopaniṣad 6.alt: A peaceful person seated at the edge of a woodland clearing, with a deer, small birds, trees and other people sharing the same soft reflected light in a still pond. No central figure dominates the other beings. Evoke seeing all beings in the Self and the Self in all, without rejection or aversion.

Īśopaniṣad 7.alt: A person with a relaxed, quietly joyful expression among a small diverse gathering of people, a deer and birds beside a river; their many reflections meet in one unbroken expanse of water. An unobtrusive scene of unity dissolving sorrow and separation. No halos identifying any one human as the supreme Self.

Īśopaniṣad 8.alt: Pure, formless diffuse light permeates an ordered natural landscape of water, stone, growing plants, sky and stars fading into morning. No human or divine body at the center: brightness without physical form, purity, self-existence and an enduring order. Detailed natural watercolor rather than a geometric diagram.

Īśopaniṣad 9.alt: Two narrow footpaths disappear into the same deep twilight forest: on one side abandoned ritual implements without understanding, on the other an isolated closed manuscript without lived engagement. A small balanced open clearing remains possible between them. Symbolic caution about one-sided avidya and vidya, not a claim that learning or ritual is evil. No labels or moral caricatures.

Īśopaniṣad 10.alt: An elderly forest teacher speaks gently to two attentive pupils in a quiet grove. Beside one pupil rests a simple tool for practical work; beside the other an open palm-leaf manuscript. Both listen equally to a nuanced teaching about the different fruits of vidya and avidya. No written marks legible on the manuscript.

Īśopaniṣad 11.alt: A single traveler crosses a modest river footbridge while carrying a simple work tool and a closed palm-leaf manuscript together, with both hands balanced. The near bank has seasonal fallen leaves; the far bank holds enduring morning light. Symbolic integration of knowledge and action, crossing mortality toward the deathless; no literal supernatural portal.

Īśopaniṣad 12.alt: A misty grove of emerging shoots, mature trees and decaying wood, with one observer focused only on a single fallen branch and another focused only on a blooming tree; both lose sight of the whole living grove in deep twilight. Evoke the warning against exclusive fixation on the unmanifest or manifest, using an open-ended contemplative metaphor rather than a doctrinal diagram.

Īśopaniṣad 13.alt: A forest sage teaches a small pair of attentive pupils beside a seed, a growing sapling and an old fallen trunk, all belonging to one natural cycle. The teacher gestures openly toward the whole scene, explaining that manifestation and the unmanifest have different fruits. No invented deity or printed explanation.

Īśopaniṣad 14.alt: A quiet riverbank holds an old fallen tree nourishing a vigorous new sapling, with a modest person observing the single continuous life of the grove. Soft light beyond the river evokes what endures while forms arise and pass away. Symbolic understanding of arising and dissolution together, passing mortality toward the deathless; no resurrection or literal immortal body.

Īśopaniṣad 15.alt: A radiant golden sun disk partially veiled by a thin luminous sheet of cloud, with a narrow opening revealing clear white-gold light beyond. A small contemplative observer below looks upward with reverence. Evoke the golden covering over the face of truth and the prayer to Pushan to uncover it; no giant human face or text in the sun.

Īśopaniṣad 16.alt: Warm rays of the sun gather into a quiet clear center above a small contemplative figure in an open landscape. The person and the distant sunlight share a gentle continuous glow, expressing recognition rather than separation. Evoke the prayer to Pushan, the sun, to gather its rays and reveal the auspicious form, and recognition of unity. No anthropomorphic face inside the sun.

Īśopaniṣad 17.alt: A gentle breeze moves dry leaves over a small, cold, clean patch of pale ash near an extinguished ceremonial hearth. The open sky continues above a calm river; a faint trail of air is suggested only by moving leaves. Evoke breath returning to immortal air, the body to ashes, and remembrance of deeds, without depicting a dying person, corpse, cremation or distress.

Īśopaniṣad 18.alt: A small steady sacred flame beside a winding forest path lights the safe way toward a clear dawn horizon, while a crooked dark side-path fades into undergrowth. A modest traveler follows the well-lit path with folded hands. Evoke the closing prayer to Agni to guide by the good path and turn away crooked wrongdoing. No battle, no fiery destruction, no text.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.1: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, assembled on the sacred field of Kurukshetra, eager to fight — what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?

Bhagavad Gītā 1.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.2: Sanjaya said: Then King Duryodhana, seeing the Pandava army arrayed in battle formation, approached his teacher Drona and spoke these words.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.3: O Teacher, behold this great army of Pandu's sons, arrayed for battle by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.4: Here are great archers equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata, and the great warrior Drupada.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.5: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best of men —

Bhagavad Gītā 1.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.6: The valiant Yudhamanyu, the powerful Uttamauja, the son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu), and the five sons of Draupadi — all of these are great warriors (maharathas).

Bhagavad Gītā 1.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.7: O best of brahmanas (Drona), know also those who are distinguished on our side. I name the commanders of my army for your information.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.8: Yourself (Drona), Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa, ever victorious in battle; Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta (Bhurishrava) —

Bhagavad Gītā 1.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.9: And many other heroes who are ready to give up their lives for my sake — equipped with various weapons, all skilled in warfare.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.10: Our army, protected by Bhishma, is unlimited (invincible); whereas their army, protected by Bhima, is limited (conquerable).

Bhagavad Gītā 1.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.11: Therefore, stationed in your respective positions at all the fronts, all of you must surely protect Bhishma alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.12: Then, to hearten him (Duryodhana), the aged grandsire of the Kurus — the mighty Bhishma — roared like a lion and blew his conch with great power.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.13: Then conches, kettledrums, tabors, trumpets, and horns — all suddenly sounded together, and that noise became tumultuous.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.14: Then Krishna (Madhava) and Arjuna (the Pandava), standing in their great chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conches.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.15: Krishna (Hrishikesha) blew his conch Panchajanya; Arjuna (Dhananjaya) blew his conch Devadatta; and the great-bellied Bhima (Vrikodara), of terrible deeds, blew his mighty conch Paundra.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.16: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew his conch Anantavijaya; while Nakula and Sahadeva blew their conches Sughosha and Manipushpaka respectively.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.17: The great archer of Kashi, the great warrior Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unconquered Satyaki —

Bhagavad Gītā 1.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.18: O lord of the earth (Dhritarashtra), Drupada, the sons of Draupadi, and the mighty-armed son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu) — all of these blew their conches separately, each one after another.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.19: That tumultuous sound, resonating through heaven and earth, tore asunder the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons (the Kauravas).

Bhagavad Gītā 1.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.20: Then, seeing Dhritarashtra's sons arrayed for battle, as weapons were about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna) — whose flag bore the emblem of a monkey — raised his bow.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.21: Arjuna said: O Achyuta (infallible one), place my chariot between the two armies.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.22: So that I may observe those who stand here ready for battle, eager to fight — with whom must I contend in this military venture?

Bhagavad Gītā 1.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.23: I wish to see those who have assembled here, ready to fight, wishing to please the evil-minded Duryodhana in battle.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.24: Sanjaya said: O Bharata (Dhritarashtra), thus addressed by Gudakesha (Arjuna), Hrishikesha positioned the excellent chariot in the middle of the two armies.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.25: In the presence of Bhishma, Drona, and all the kings of the earth, (Krishna) said: O Partha, behold these assembled Kurus.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.26: There, Partha saw standing in both armies: fathers and grandfathers, teachers and maternal uncles, brothers and sons, grandsons and companions.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.27: And fathers-in-law and dear friends in both armies — seeing all these kinsmen thus assembled, that son of Kunti (Arjuna) —

Bhagavad Gītā 1.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.28: Overcome with utmost compassion, sorrowful, he (Arjuna) said: O Krishna, seeing my own people assembled here, eager for battle —

Bhagavad Gītā 1.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.29: My limbs are giving way, my mouth is drying up, my body is trembling, and my hair is standing on end.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.30: The Gandiva (bow) slips from my hand, my skin is burning, I am unable to stand, and my mind seems to whirl.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.31: O Keshava, I see ill omens and I perceive no good (shreya) in killing my own people in battle.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.32: O Krishna, I desire neither victory nor kingdom nor pleasures. O Govinda, what is a kingdom to us? What are enjoyments? What even is life itself?

Bhagavad Gītā 1.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.33: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures — they themselves stand here in battle, having renounced their lives and wealth.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.34: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other kinsmen —

Bhagavad Gītā 1.35.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.35: O Madhusudana, I do not wish to kill these men even if they kill me — not for lordship over the three worlds, let alone for the sake of this earth.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.36.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.36: O Janardana, what joy would come to us from killing Dhritarashtra's sons? Only sin would cling to us from slaying these aggressors.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.37.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.37: Therefore, O Madhava, we are not justified in killing our own kinsmen, Dhritarashtra's sons. How indeed could we be happy after slaying our own people?

Bhagavad Gītā 1.38.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.38: Even if these men — their minds overcome by greed — do not perceive the wrong incurred by destroying a family and the sin of betraying friends —

Bhagavad Gītā 1.39.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.39: O Janardana, how should we — who clearly see the wrong in the destruction of a family — not know to turn back from this sin?

Bhagavad Gītā 1.40.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.40: When a family is destroyed, its eternal family traditions perish; when tradition perishes, adharma overtakes the entire family.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.41.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.41: O Krishna, when adharma prevails, the women of the family become corrupted; O Vārṣṇeya, when women are corrupted, there arises the intermixing of social orders (varṇa-saṃkara).

Bhagavad Gītā 1.42.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.42: This intermixing leads to hell for the destroyers of the family and for the family itself. Indeed, their ancestors fall, deprived of the offerings of rice-balls and water.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.43.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.43: By these wrongs of the family-destroyers — wrongs that cause the intermixing of social orders — the eternal traditions of social duty (jāti-dharma) and family duty (kula-dharma) are uprooted.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.44.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.44: O Janardana, we have heard that men whose family traditions are destroyed must dwell in hell for an indeterminate time.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.45.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.45: Alas, what a great sin we are resolved to commit — that out of greed for the pleasures of kingship, we are prepared to kill our own people.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.46.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.46: It would be more beneficial for me if the armed sons of Dhritarashtra were to kill me in battle, unresisting and unarmed.

Bhagavad Gītā 1.47.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.47: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus in the midst of battle, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief, casting aside his bow and arrows.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.1: Sanjaya said: To him who was thus overcome with compassion, whose eyes were filled with tears and in distress, Madhusudana spoke these words.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.2: The Blessed Lord said: O Arjuna, from where has this faint-heartedness (kaśmala) come upon you at this critical moment? It is unbecoming of an Ārya, does not lead to heaven, and brings infamy.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.3: O Partha, do not yield to unmanliness — it does not befit you. O scorcher of foes (Parantapa), shake off this faint-heartedness and rise.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.4: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, O destroyer of enemies, how shall I fight in battle against Bhishma and Drona — who are worthy of my reverence — with arrows?

Bhagavad Gītā 2.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.5: It is better in this world to beg for sustenance than to kill these great and noble teachers. If I slay them, all the pleasures I would enjoy here would be stained with blood.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.6: We do not know which is better for us — that we should conquer them or that they should conquer us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us; having slain them, we would not wish to live.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.7: My nature is overcome by the fault of faint-heartedness; my mind is confused about dharma. I ask you: tell me with certainty what is truly better for me. I am your disciple; teach me, who has taken refuge in you.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.8: I do not see what could remove this grief that dries up my senses — even if I were to attain unrivalled, prosperous dominion on earth, or even lordship over the gods.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.9: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha — the scorcher of enemies — said to Govinda 'I will not fight,' and fell silent.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.10: O Bharata (Dhritarashtra), Hrishikesha, as if smiling, spoke these words to him who was grief-stricken between the two armies.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.11: The Blessed Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.12: There was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.13: Just as in this body the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age, so too it passes into another body. The wise person is not deluded by this.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.14: O Kaunteya, the contacts between the senses and their objects give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go, they are impermanent — endure them, O Bharata.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.15: O best of men (Puruṣarṣabha), the wise person whom these (sense contacts) do not disturb — steady in pain and pleasure — becomes fit for immortality (amṛtatva).

Bhagavad Gītā 2.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.16: The unreal has no being; the real never ceases to be. The conclusion about both these has been perceived by the seers of truth.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.17: Know that by which this entire universe is pervaded to be indestructible. No one is capable of destroying this imperishable one.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.18: These bodies of the eternal, indestructible, immeasurable embodied Self are said to have an end. Therefore, O Bharata, fight.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.19: He who thinks this (Self) to be the slayer and he who thinks it to be slain — both of these do not know. It neither slays nor is it slain.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.20: This (Self) is never born, nor does it ever die; nor having once been, does it cease to be. It is unborn, eternal, ever-existing, and ancient. It is not slain when the body is slain.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.21: O Partha, he who knows this Self to be indestructible, eternal, unborn, and inexhaustible — how can that person kill anyone or cause anyone to be killed?

Bhagavad Gītā 2.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.22: Just as a person puts on new garments after discarding the worn-out ones, similarly the embodied Self (dehī) casts off worn-out bodies and takes on other new ones.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.23: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.24: This Self is uncleavable, incombustible, neither to be wetted nor dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable, and everlasting.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.25: This Self is said to be unmanifest, unthinkable, and unchangeable. Therefore, knowing it as such, you should not grieve.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.26: But even if you think of this Self as perpetually born and perpetually dying, O mighty-armed one, even then you should not grieve like this.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.27: For the born, death is certain; and for the dead, birth is certain. Therefore you should not grieve over what is inevitable.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.28: O Bharata, beings are unmanifest before birth, manifest in the middle (during life), and unmanifest again after death — what lamentation is there in this?

Bhagavad Gītā 2.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.29: Someone sees this Self as a wonder; another speaks of it as a wonder; another hears of it as a wonder — yet even after hearing, no one truly knows it.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.30: O Bharata, this embodied Self (dehī) dwelling in the bodies of all is eternally indestructible. Therefore you should not grieve for any being.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.31: Furthermore, looking at your own dharma, you should not waver; for a kṣatriya, there is nothing more auspicious than a righteous war.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.32: O Partha, fortunate are the kṣatriyas who encounter such a battle, which has come of itself, opening the very gates of heaven.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.33: But if you do not fight this righteous battle, then having abandoned your own dharma and glory, you will incur sin.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.34: People will speak of your imperishable infamy; and for one who has been honoured, disgrace is worse than death.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.35.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.35: The great warriors will think that you have withdrawn from battle out of fear; and you will fall from esteem among those who have held you in high regard.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.36.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.36: Your enemies will speak many unspeakable words, deriding your ability. What could be more painful than that?

Bhagavad Gītā 2.37.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.37: If slain, you will attain heaven; if victorious, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, O son of Kunti, rise up with firm resolve for battle.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.38.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.38: Having made pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat equal, engage in battle. In this way you will not incur sin.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.39.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.39: O Partha, this understanding has been declared to you in terms of Sānkhya; now hear it in terms of Yoga — endowed with which understanding, you shall completely break free from the bondage of karma.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.40.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.40: In this (Yoga) there is no loss of the initiative, nor is there any adverse result. Even a little practice of this dharma protects one from great fear.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.41.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.41: O joy of the Kurus, in this path the resolute understanding is single and one-pointed; but the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.42.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.42: O Partha, those who are undiscerning, who are devoted to the letter of the Vedas and declare that there is nothing else — they proclaim this flowery speech.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.43.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.43: Desirous of pleasures and heavenly reward, proclaiming rebirths as the fruit of actions, filled with various special rites aimed at attaining enjoyment and lordship —

Bhagavad Gītā 2.44.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.44: For those who are deeply attached to pleasure and power, whose minds have been carried away by such (flowery) speech — for them, the resolute, one-pointed understanding does not arise in meditation.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.45.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.45: The Vedas deal with the three guṇas (qualities of nature). Be free of the three guṇas, O Arjuna — free from the pairs of opposites, ever established in sattva, unconcerned with getting and keeping, and established in the Self.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.46.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.46: As much use as there is in a small well when there is a flood of water on all sides — so much is the use of all the Vedas for a brāhmaṇa who has gained true knowledge.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.47.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.47: Your right is to action alone; never to its fruits at any time. Do not be motivated by the fruits of action; nor let there be attachment to inaction.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.48.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.48: O Dhananjaya, perform actions while established in Yoga, abandoning attachment, being equal in success and failure. Equanimity (samatva) is called Yoga.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.49.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.49: Far inferior to Buddhi-yoga is action motivated by results, O Dhananjaya. Seek refuge in the buddhi. Those who are motivated by fruits are miserly.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.50.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.50: One endowed with Buddhi-yoga casts off both good and evil deeds here itself. Therefore, yoke yourself to Yoga. Yoga is skill in actions.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.51.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.51: The wise endowed with Buddhi-yoga, abandoning the fruits born of action, are freed from the bondage of birth and attain the state that is free from all affliction.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.52.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.52: When your intellect will cross the thicket of delusion, then you will attain dispassion (nirveda) toward what has been heard and what is yet to be heard.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.53.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.53: When your intellect — scattered by the conflicting declarations of the scriptures — will stand immovable and unwavering in samādhi, then you will attain Yoga.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.54.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.54: Arjuna said: O Keshava, what is the description of one of steady wisdom established in samādhi? How does the sthita-dhī speak? How does he sit? How does he walk?

Bhagavad Gītā 2.55.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.55: The Blessed Lord said: O Partha, when one completely abandons all desires dwelling in the mind and is satisfied in the Self alone by the Self — then one is called sthita-prajña (one of steady wisdom).

Bhagavad Gītā 2.56.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.56: One whose mind is not agitated in adversity, who has no craving in prosperity, who is free from attachment, fear, and anger — such a one is called a muni of steady wisdom.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.57.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.57: One who is without attachment everywhere, who neither rejoices on obtaining good nor feels aversion on getting evil — his wisdom is firmly established.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.58.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.58: When, like a tortoise withdrawing its limbs on all sides, one withdraws the senses from the sense-objects — then his wisdom is firmly established.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.59.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.59: For one who restrains the senses from objects, the objects turn away, but the taste (rasa) for them remains. Even this taste departs for one who has seen the Supreme.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.60.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.60: O son of Kunti, even for the wise person who strives, the turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.61.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.61: Having restrained all of them (the senses), one should sit with Me as the Supreme (mat-paraḥ). For whose senses are under control, his wisdom is firmly established.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.62.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.62: In one who dwells on sense-objects, attachment to them arises; from attachment, desire is born; from desire, anger is born.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.63.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.63: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, loss of memory; from loss of memory, destruction of the intellect; from destruction of the intellect, one is completely ruined.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.64.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.64: But one who moves among sense-objects with senses freed from attraction and aversion, self-controlled, with the self mastered — attains inner serenity (prasāda).

Bhagavad Gītā 2.65.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.65: Upon attaining serenity (prasāda), all sorrow disappears for this person. Indeed, the intellect of one with a serene mind quickly becomes well-established.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.66.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.66: For the undisciplined (ayukta), there is no wisdom; for the undisciplined, there is no contemplative power (bhāvanā); for one without contemplation, there is no peace; and for the peaceless, how can there be happiness?

Bhagavad Gītā 2.67.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.67: For when the mind follows any one of the roaming senses, it carries away his wisdom — just as the wind carries away a boat on water.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.68.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.68: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, the wisdom (prajñā) of one who has fully withdrawn the senses from their objects in every way is firmly established.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.69.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.69: What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one (saṃyamī) is awake; what all beings are awake to, that is night for the seeing sage (muni).

Bhagavad Gītā 2.70.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.70: Just as waters flow into the ocean, which though ever being filled remains unmoved and within its bounds — so too the one into whom all desires enter (and are absorbed) attains peace; not the one who keeps desiring desires.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.71.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.71: The person who, having abandoned all desires, moves through life free of longing (niḥspṛha), free of the sense of 'mine' (nirmama), and free of ego (nirahaṃkāra) — that person attains peace.

Bhagavad Gītā 2.72.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.72: O Pārtha, this is the Brāhmī state (the state of Brahman). Having attained it, one is never again deluded. Being established in it even at the moment of death, one reaches Brahma-nirvāṇa — absorption in Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.1: Arjuna said: O Janardana, if You consider knowledge (buddhi) to be superior to action, then why do You urge me to this terrible action (war), O Keshava?

Bhagavad Gītā 3.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.2: With seemingly mixed words, You confuse my intellect. Therefore, tell me decisively that one thing by which I may attain the highest good (śreya).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.3: The Blessed Lord said: O sinless one (Anagha), two paths of devotion have been expounded by Me from ancient times in this world — the path of knowledge (jñāna-yoga) for the contemplative (sāṃkhya), and the path of action (karma-yoga) for the active (yogin).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.4: A person does not attain freedom from the bondage of action (naiṣkarmya) by merely refraining from action; nor does he attain perfection (siddhi) merely by renouncing action (sannyāsa).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.5: Indeed, no one can remain even for a moment without performing action; for all beings are helplessly impelled to action by the guṇas born of prakṛti.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.6: One who outwardly restrains the organs of action while inwardly dwelling on sense-objects with the mind — that deluded person is called a hypocrite (mithyācāra).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.7: But one who, controlling the senses through the mind, O Arjuna, engages the organs of action in Karma-yoga without attachment — that person is superior.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.8: Perform your prescribed duty (niyata karma); action is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of your body cannot be accomplished without action.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.9: This world is bound by action except when action is performed as sacrifice (yajña). O Kaunteya, perform action for that purpose (yajña), free from attachment.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.10: In ancient times, the Lord of Creatures (Prajāpati) created humankind together with sacrifice (yajña) and said: 'By this shall you prosper; let this be the fulfiller of all your desired wishes (iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk).'

Bhagavad Gītā 3.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.11: Nourish the devas (divine powers) with this sacrifice; let those devas nourish you. Nourishing one another, you shall attain the highest good (paraṃ śreya).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.12: Nourished by sacrifice, the devas will indeed give you your desired enjoyments. One who enjoys their gifts without offering back to them is verily a thief.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.13: The righteous, who eat the remnants of sacrifice (yajña-śiṣṭa), are freed from all sins. But those sinful ones who cook only for themselves — they eat sin alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.14: Beings arise from food; food arises from rain; rain arises from sacrifice (yajña); sacrifice arises from action (karma).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.15: Know that action (karma) arises from the Vedas (Brahman); and the Vedas arise from the Imperishable (Akṣara, the Absolute). Therefore, the all-pervading Brahman is eternally established in yajña.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.16: O Pārtha, one who does not follow this wheel thus set in motion in this world — living for the senses, sinful in life — lives in vain (mogham).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.17: But one who delights only in the ātman, who is satisfied only by the ātman, and who is content only in the ātman — for that person, there remains no duty to perform.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.18: For that person, there is no purpose served by action done, nor any harm from action undone. Nor does that person depend on any being for any purpose whatsoever.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.19: Therefore, always perform what must be done (kāryaṃ karma), free from attachment. For a person who acts without attachment attains the Supreme.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.20: Indeed, it was through action alone that Janaka and others attained perfection (saṃsiddhi). You should also perform action with a view to the welfare of the world (loka-saṃgraha).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.21: Whatever a great person does, others follow. Whatever standard (pramāṇa) that person sets, the world follows that.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.22: O Pārtha, there is nothing whatsoever that I need to do in the three worlds; nothing unattained that needs to be attained — yet I remain engaged in action.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.23: For, O Pārtha, if I were ever to remain without diligent action, all people would follow my path in every way.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.24: If I were not to perform action, these worlds would perish. I would be the author of confusion (saṃkara) and would destroy these beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.25: O Bhārata, just as the ignorant act with attachment to action, so should the wise act without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world (loka-saṃgraha).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.26: Let no wise person disturb the minds of the ignorant who are attached to action. Acting in a spirit of yoga, the wise one should inspire them toward all their actions (joṣayet).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.27: All actions are performed in every way by the guṇas of prakṛti (nature). The self deluded by ego thinks: 'I am the doer.'

Bhagavad Gītā 3.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.28: But one who knows the truth about the division of guṇas and karma, O mighty-armed, understanding that 'guṇas act upon guṇas,' is not attached.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.29: Those deluded by the guṇas of prakṛti become attached to the functions of the guṇas. The person of complete knowledge (kṛtsna-vit) should not unsettle those of incomplete knowledge (akṛtsna-vidas) and slow understanding.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.30: Renouncing all actions in Me, with the mind fixed on the ātman, free from hope (nirāśī), free from the sense of 'mine' (nirmama), and free from mental fever (vigata-jvara) — fight.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.31: Those persons who constantly follow this teaching of Mine with faith and without caviling — they too are freed from the bondage of karma.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.32: But those who cavil at this teaching and do not follow My instruction — know them to be deluded in all knowledge, mindless, and lost.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.33: Even a person of knowledge acts in accordance with their own nature. All beings follow their nature — what will restraint (nigraha) accomplish?

Bhagavad Gītā 3.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.34: In the objects of each sense, attraction (rāga) and aversion (dveṣa) are established. One should not come under the sway of these two, for they are one's enemies on the path.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.35.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.35: One's own dharma, though imperfectly performed, is superior to the well-performed dharma of another. Death in one's own dharma is better; the dharma of another is fraught with danger.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.36.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.36: Arjuna said: O Vārṣṇeya, then by what is a person compelled — even against their will, as if driven by force — to commit sin?

Bhagavad Gītā 3.37.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.37: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire — it is anger — born of the quality of rajas. It is all-devouring, greatly sinful. Know this as the enemy here.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.38.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.38: Just as fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb's membrane (ulba) — so is this (wisdom) covered by that (desire).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.39.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.39: O Kaunteya, the wisdom of the wise is covered by this eternal enemy — in the form of desire, which is like an insatiable fire.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.40.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.40: The senses, mind, and intellect are said to be the dwelling places of this (desire). Through these, it deludes the embodied being (dehin) by veiling its wisdom.

Bhagavad Gītā 3.41.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.41: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, first restraining the senses, slay this sinful destroyer of knowledge (jñāna) and wisdom (vijñāna).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.42.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.42: The senses are said to be superior (to the body); superior to the senses is the mind; superior to the mind is the intellect; and that which is superior even to the intellect — that is the Self (ātman).

Bhagavad Gītā 3.43.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 3.43: O mighty-armed one, thus knowing that which is beyond even the intellect (the ātman), steadying the self by the Self, slay the enemy in the form of desire — difficult to overcome.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.1: The Blessed Lord said: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvān (the Sun-god); Vivasvān told it to Manu; and Manu declared it to Ikṣvāku.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.2: In this manner, transmitted through an unbroken succession, the royal sages knew this yoga. But through the passage of a long period of time, O Parantapa, this yoga became lost in this world.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.3: That same ancient yoga has been declared by me to you today; for you are my devotee and my friend — and this is indeed the supreme secret.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.4: Arjuna said: Your birth is recent, and the birth of Vivasvān was in ancient times — how then am I to understand that you declared this yoga to him in the beginning?

Bhagavad Gītā 4.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.5: The Blessed Lord said: Many births of mine have passed, as well as yours, O Arjuna. I know them all, but you do not know them, O Parantapa.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.6: Although I am unborn and my Self is imperishable, although I am the Lord of all beings — yet by presiding over my own prakṛti, I manifest through my own māyā (yoga-śakti).

Bhagavad Gītā 4.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.7: Whenever there is a decline of dharma, O Bhārata, and a rise of adharma — then I project myself forth.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.8: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the firm establishment of righteousness — I come into being age after age.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.9: O Arjuna, one who knows my birth and action as thus divine — having left the body, he is not reborn; he comes to me.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.10: Freed from desire, fear, and anger, absorbed in me, taking refuge in me — many have been purified by the tapas of knowledge and have attained my state of being.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.11: In whatever way people take refuge in me, in that very way do I respond to them, O Pārtha. Human beings follow my path in every direction.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.12: Those who desire the fruits of their actions worship the gods here in this world; for in the human realm, success born of action comes swiftly.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.13: The fourfold order was created by me according to the division of qualities (guṇas) and action (karma). Though I am its creator, know me to be the imperishable non-doer.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.14: Actions do not taint me; nor do I have any longing for the fruits of action. One who knows me thus is not bound by actions.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.15: Even the ancient seekers of liberation performed action with this understanding. Therefore, you too perform action just as those predecessors did from ancient times.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.16: What is action and what is non-action? — Even the learned are confused about this. I shall declare to you that action, knowing which you will be freed from inauspiciousness.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.17: One must understand the nature of action, the nature of forbidden action (vikarma), and also the nature of non-action (akarma) — for the path of action is deep and difficult to understand.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.18: One who sees non-action in action and action in non-action — he is wise among humans; he is the one united in yoga, the doer of all actions.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.19: One whose every undertaking is free from desire and deliberate intention — whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge — him the wise call a paṇḍita (truly learned).

Bhagavad Gītā 4.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.20: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, always contented, depending on nothing — even while being fully engaged in action, he truly does nothing at all.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.21: Without aspiration, with mind and self restrained, having abandoned all possessiveness — performing action only for the body's sake, he incurs no sin.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.22: Content with whatever comes unsought, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, and equal in success and failure — even having acted, he is not bound.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.23: For one whose attachment is gone, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge — acting for the sake of sacrifice (yajña), his entire karma dissolves away.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.24: The instrument of offering is Brahman; the oblation is Brahman; Brahman offers into the fire of Brahman — Brahman alone is to be reached by one who is absorbed in Brahman-action.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.25: Some yogīs offer worship to the deities as sacrifice; others offer the sacrifice itself into the fire of Brahman by means of sacrifice.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.26: Others offer the senses — hearing and the rest — into the fires of self-restraint; others offer sound and other sense-objects into the fires of the senses.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.27: Others offer all the activities of the senses and all the activities of the vital breath (prāṇa) into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.28: Some ascetics, who are of sharpened vows, perform the sacrifice of material wealth (dravya-yajña), the sacrifice of austerity (tapo-yajña), and the sacrifice of yoga (yoga-yajña); others perform the sacrifice of scriptural study (svādhyāya) and the sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña).

Bhagavad Gītā 4.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.29: Those devoted to prāṇāyāma offer the outgoing breath (prāṇa) into the incoming breath (apāna), and the incoming into the outgoing; and having restrained the movement of both prāṇa and apāna, they are fixed in breath retention.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.30: Others, who have regulated their diet, offer prāṇas into prāṇas. All these, indeed, are knowers of sacrifice, and their impurities (sins) have been destroyed by sacrifice.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.31: Those who eat the nectar-like remnant of sacrifice go to the eternal Brahman. This world is not (joyful) for one who performs no sacrifice, O best of Kurus — how then the next world?

Bhagavad Gītā 4.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.32: Thus many kinds of sacrifices are spread out in the mouth of Brahman (the Vedas). Know them all to be born from action; knowing this thus, you shall be liberated.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.33: Superior to the sacrifice made of material wealth is the sacrifice of knowledge, O Parantapa. All action in its entirety, O Pārtha, reaches its culmination and fulfillment in knowledge.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.34: Know that (knowledge) by prostration (praṇipāta), by sincere questioning (paripraśna), and by service (sevā); the wise who are seers of truth will teach you that knowledge.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.35.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.35: Knowing which, O Pāṇḍava, you shall not again fall into delusion like this — and by which you shall see all beings without exception in the Self, and then in Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.36.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.36: Even if you were the most sinful of all sinners, you shall indeed cross the entire ocean of sin by the boat of knowledge alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.37.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.37: Just as a blazing fire reduces its fuel (kindling) to ashes, O Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge reduces all karma to ashes in the same way.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.38.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.38: Truly, nothing in this world is as purifying as knowledge. One who is perfected in yoga discovers it by himself within the Self in due course of time.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.39.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.39: One who has faith, who is devoted to it, and who has mastered the senses, attains knowledge; having attained knowledge, he quickly reaches supreme peace.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.40.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.40: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting self perishes. For the doubting self there is neither this world, nor the next, nor any happiness.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.41.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.41: Actions do not bind one who has renounced actions through yoga, whose doubts have been completely severed by knowledge, and who is established in the Self, O Dhanañjaya.

Bhagavad Gītā 4.42.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.42: Therefore, having cut with the sword of Self-knowledge this doubt born of ignorance, which dwells in your heart — stand firm in yoga and rise up, O Bhārata!

Bhagavad Gītā 5.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.1: Arjuna said: O Krishna, You praise renunciation of actions and then also the yoga of action. Tell me with certainty which one of these two is better.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.2: The Blessed Lord said: Both renunciation and the yoga of action lead to the highest good. But of the two, karma yoga is superior to the renunciation of action.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.3: He should be known as a perpetual renunciant who neither hates nor desires. For, free from all dualities, O mighty-armed, he is easily liberated from bondage.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.4: Children, not the wise, declare Sāṃkhya and Yoga to be different. One who is properly established in even one of them obtains the fruit of both.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.5: The state attained by the Sāṃkhyas is also reached by the Yogis. He who sees Sāṃkhya and Yoga as one — he truly sees.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.6: But renunciation, O mighty-armed, is difficult to attain without yoga. The sage who is united through yoga reaches Brahman without delay.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.7: One who is united in yoga, pure in heart, master of the self, with senses controlled, and who sees his own Self in all beings — though acting, he is not bound.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.8: The one who is united, who knows the truth, thinks 'I do nothing at all' — even while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, and breathing.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.9: Even while speaking, releasing, grasping, opening or closing the eyes — holding firm the conviction that 'the senses are moving among their sense-objects; I am not doing.'

Bhagavad Gītā 5.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.10: One who acts by offering all actions to Brahman, abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.11: Yogis perform action by body, mind, intellect, and even by the senses alone, having abandoned attachment — for the purification of the self.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.12: The one who is united abandons the fruit of action and attains lasting peace. The one who is not united, driven by desire, attached to results, is bound.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.13: Having renounced all actions mentally, the self-controlled embodied one dwells happily in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing action.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.14: The Lord (the Self) neither creates the agency of people, nor their actions, nor the connection of action with its fruit. It is nature (svabhāva) that moves and acts.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.15: The all-pervading Lord neither takes on anyone's sin nor their merit. Knowledge is veiled by ignorance — that is why creatures fall into delusion.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.16: But for those whose ignorance of the Self has been destroyed by knowledge, that knowledge, like the sun, illuminates the supreme truth.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.17: Those whose intellect is absorbed in That, whose very self is That, whose steadfastness is in That, whose supreme goal is That — their impurities cleansed by knowledge, they go to non-return.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.18: The wise see with equal vision a learned and humble brāhmaṇa, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and even an outcast (dog-cooker).

Bhagavad Gītā 5.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.19: Even here, by those whose minds are established in equality, the entire creation is conquered. Since Brahman is flawless and equal, they are therefore established in Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.20: One who does not rejoice on obtaining the pleasant, nor becomes troubled on obtaining the unpleasant — such a one is of steady intellect, undeluded, a knower of Brahman, established in Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.21: One whose inner self is unattached to external sense-contacts finds the joy that is in the Self. That one, whose self is united in Brahma-yoga, tastes imperishable joy.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.22: The enjoyments born of sense-contact are sources of sorrow alone, O son of Kuntī. They have a beginning and an end — the wise do not delight in them.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.23: One who can withstand, even here in this life, before liberation from the body, the impulse born of desire and anger — that one is integrated (yukta), that one is a happy person.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.24: One who is happy within, who finds delight within, who is illumined within — that yogi, becoming Brahman, attains nirvāṇa in Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.25: Seers who have eliminated their impurities, whose doubts have been cut through, who are self-restrained, and who are devoted to the welfare of all beings — they attain nirvāṇa in Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.26: For the self-disciplined ascetics who are free from desire and anger, who have restrained the mind and have known the Self — brahma-nirvāṇa surrounds them on all sides.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.27: Having excluded external sense-contacts, fixing the gaze between the two eyebrows, having equalized the inward and outward breaths moving within the nostrils —

Bhagavad Gītā 5.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.28: The sage who has controlled the senses, mind, and intellect, who is intent on liberation, who is free from desire, fear, and anger — such a one is always and forever free.

Bhagavad Gītā 5.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 5.29: Knowing Me as the enjoyer of all sacrifices and austerities, the Great Lord of all worlds, and the selfless friend of all beings — one attains peace.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.1: The Blessed Lord said: One who performs the action that ought to be done without depending on the fruit of action — that person is both a sannyāsī and a yogī. Not the one who has abandoned fire, nor the one who has abandoned action.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.2: O Pāṇḍava! Know that what they call sannyāsa is what is called yoga. For without renouncing the saṅkalpas (desires, intentions), no one ever becomes a yogi.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.3: For the sage who desires to ascend to yoga, action is said to be the means. For the same person who has already ascended to yoga, stillness (śama) is said to be the means.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.4: When one is no longer attached to sense-objects and no longer attached to actions, then one who has renounced all saṅkalpas (desires, intentions) is said to have ascended to yoga.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.5: Let a person uplift oneself by the self; let one not degrade oneself. The self alone is the friend of the self; the self alone is the enemy of the self.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.6: For the one who has conquered the self by the self, the self is a friend. But for one who has not conquered the self, the self acts as an enemy in the manner of a foe.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.7: For the one who has conquered the self and is deeply at peace, the Paramātman is integrated (steadily present) — in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honour and dishonour.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.8: One whose inner self is satisfied by knowledge and direct realization, who is immovable, self-controlled in the senses, and who regards a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal — such a yogi is called 'yukta' (perfectly integrated).

Bhagavad Gītā 6.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.9: One who maintains equal-mindedness toward a well-wisher, a friend, an enemy, a neutral, an arbitrator, the hateful, and one's own kin — as well as toward the righteous and the sinful — such a one is distinguished (spiritually pre-eminent).

Bhagavad Gītā 6.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.10: Let the yogi continuously engage the self in yoga, stationed in solitude, alone, with mind and body restrained, free from hope and free from accumulation.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.11: Having established a firm seat for oneself in a clean place — neither too high nor too low — with cloth, deerskin, and kuśa grass layered upon it.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.12: Having sat on that seat, with mind made one-pointed, with the functions of mind and senses restrained — let one practise yoga there for the purification of the self.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.13: Holding the body, head, and neck erect and still, steady, gazing at the tip of one's nose and not looking in any other direction —

Bhagavad Gītā 6.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.14: With a serene inner self, free from fear, established in the vow of brahmacarya, with the mind controlled — let one sit integrated, with consciousness in Me, devoted to Me as the supreme.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.15: Continuously engaging the self in yoga thus, the yogi of restrained mind attains the peace that culminates in nirvāṇa — established in Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.16: O Arjuna, yoga is not for the one who eats too much, nor for the one who eats nothing at all. Nor for the one who sleeps too much, nor for the one who is always awake.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.17: For one who is measured in eating and recreation, measured in effort in actions, measured in sleep and wakefulness — yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.18: When the disciplined mind rests in the Self alone, free from longing for all objects of desire — then that person is called 'yukta' (perfectly integrated, yoga-united).

Bhagavad Gītā 6.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.19: As a lamp placed in a windless spot does not flicker — that is the simile recalled for the yogi of restrained mind who practises yoga of the Self.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.20: The state where the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, becomes quiescent — and where seeing the Self by the Self alone, one is satisfied within the Self.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.21: The transcendent joy that is known there — graspable by the intellect yet beyond the senses — once established in that state, one does not move from the truth.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.22: Obtaining which, one does not consider any other gain to be greater, and being established in which, one is not moved even by the deepest sorrow.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.23: Let one know that which is called yoga to be the disjunction from the conjunction with sorrow. That yoga is to be practised with determination and with a mind that does not lose heart.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.24: Abandoning completely and without remainder all desires born of saṅkalpa, and restraining the entire company of senses by the mind alone on every side —

Bhagavad Gītā 6.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.25: Gradually, step by step, let one attain stillness through the intellect endowed with patience; having made the mind established in the Self, let one not think of anything at all.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.26: Wherever the restless and unsteady mind wanders, from there, having restrained it, let one bring it back again and again into the Self alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.27: Supreme happiness comes to this yogi whose mind is deeply at peace, whose rajas is pacified, who has become Brahman, and who is free from all impurity.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.28: Thus continuously engaging the self in yoga, the yogi who is free from impurity easily attains the transcendent joy of brahma-saṃsparśa — contact with Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.29: The yoga-united self who sees everywhere equally perceives the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.30: One who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me — I am never lost to that one, and that one is never lost to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.31: One who, established in oneness, worships Me dwelling in all beings — that yogi, in whatever way they live, dwells in Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.32: O Arjuna, one who sees everywhere with equality — by the measure of the Self — whether in pleasure or in pain — that yogi is considered supreme.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.33: Arjuna said: O Madhusūdana, this yoga of equanimity that You have described — I do not see a stable, lasting footing for it, due to the mind's restlessness.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.34: O Krishna, the mind is indeed restless, turbulent, powerful, and stubborn. I consider its restraint as difficult as restraining the wind.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.35.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.35: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed, the mind is restless and difficult to restrain. But O son of Kuntī, it is brought under control by practice and by dispassion.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.36.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.36: For one of uncontrolled self (mind), yoga is difficult to attain — such is my view. But for the self-controlled, striving person who uses the right means, it is possible to attain.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.37.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.37: Arjuna said: O Krishna, the one who is endowed with faith yet lacking in effort, whose mind has strayed from yoga — not having attained perfection in yoga, what end does that one reach?

Bhagavad Gītā 6.38.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.38: O mighty-armed, does that one not perish like a torn cloud — fallen from both, without support, bewildered on the path to Brahman?

Bhagavad Gītā 6.39.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.39: O Krishna, You alone are fit to dispel this doubt of mine completely. No one other than You is fit to cut through this doubt.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.40.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.40: The Blessed Lord said: O Pārtha, neither in this world nor in the next does destruction come to that one. My dear one (tāta), one who does good never comes to an evil end.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.41.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.41: The fallen yogi attains the worlds of the meritorious, dwelling there for immeasurable years, and then takes birth in the home of the pure and prosperous.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.42.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.42: Or else one takes birth in the very family of wise yogis — for such a birth as this is truly very rare in the world.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.43.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.43: There, that one regains the intellectual connection (buddhi-saṃyoga) from the previous body, and strives even further toward perfection, O joy of the Kurus.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.44.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.44: By that very previous practice, he is carried along irresistibly — even without his will. Even one who merely inquires about yoga transcends the Verbal Brahman (the Vedic rituals).

Bhagavad Gītā 6.45.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.45: But the yogi who strives with effort, whose sins have been thoroughly purified, and who has been perfected over many births — then attains the supreme goal.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.46.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.46: A yogi is superior to ascetics, superior even to those of knowledge, and superior to ritual performers. Therefore, O Arjuna, be a yogi.

Bhagavad Gītā 6.47.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 6.47: And among all yogis, the one who worships Me with inner self absorbed in Me, filled with faith — that one is considered by Me to be the most perfectly integrated (yuktatama).

Bhagavad Gītā 7.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.1: The Blessed Lord said: O Pārtha, with mind attached to Me, practicing yoga taking refuge in Me — hear how you shall know Me completely and without doubt.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.2: I will declare to you this knowledge (jñāna) along with wisdom (vijñāna) completely, without remainder — knowing which, nothing else here remains to be known.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.3: Among thousands of human beings, perhaps one strives for perfection (siddhi); and among those who strive and succeed, perhaps one knows Me in truth (tattvataḥ).

Bhagavad Gītā 7.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.4: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego — this is My nature divided eightfold, the lower nature (aparā prakṛti).

Bhagavad Gītā 7.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.5: O mighty-armed one, this (aparā) is the lower nature. Know My other nature — the higher (parā), which is the life-principle (jīva-bhūtā), by which this entire world is sustained.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.6: Know that all beings have their womb (origin) in these two natures. I am the source (prabhava) and dissolution (pralaya) of the entire universe.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.7: O Dhananjaya, there is nothing whatsoever higher than Me. All this is strung on Me as pearls are strung on a thread.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.8: O Kaunteya, I am the taste in water, the light in the moon and sun; I am the sacred syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in ether, and the virility in human beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.9: I am the sacred fragrance of the earth and the brilliance in fire; I am the life in all beings and the austerity (tapas) in ascetics.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.10: Know Me as the eternal seed of all beings, O Pārtha. I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the brilliance of the brilliant.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.11: O best of the Bharatas, I am the strength of the strong that is devoid of desire and passion; and in beings I am the desire that is not opposed to dharma.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.12: Whatever states exist — sāttvic, rājasic, and tāmasic — know that all of them proceed from Me alone. Yet I am not in them; they are in Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.13: Deluded by these three guṇa-constituted states, this entire world fails to recognize Me — who am beyond them, imperishable (avyaya).

Bhagavad Gītā 7.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.14: Indeed, this divine māyā of Mine, constituted of the guṇas, is difficult to cross. But those who take refuge in Me alone — they cross beyond this māyā.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.15: The evildoers, the foolish, the lowest among men, those whose wisdom has been stripped by māyā, and those who have taken refuge in the demonic nature — they do not take refuge in Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.16: O Bharatarṣabha Arjuna, four kinds of virtuous people (sukṛtinaḥ) worship Me: the distressed (ārta), the seeker of knowledge (jijñāsu), the seeker of wealth (arthārthī), and the wise (jñānī).

Bhagavad Gītā 7.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.17: Of these, the jñānī who is ever-united (nitya-yukta) and of single-pointed devotion (eka-bhakti) is distinguished. For I am exceedingly dear to the jñānī, and that one is exceedingly dear to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.18: All of these are indeed noble; but the jñānī, I hold, is My very Self. For that one, with a unified mind (yuktātmā), abides in Me alone as the supreme goal (anuttamāṃ gatim).

Bhagavad Gītā 7.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.19: At the end of many births, the one possessed of knowledge (jñānavān) takes refuge in Me, realizing 'Vāsudeva is all.' Such a great soul (mahātmā) is exceedingly rare.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.20: Those whose wisdom has been carried away by various desires take refuge in other gods, following this or that rule (of worship), governed by their own nature.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.21: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith — I make that same faith of that devotee unwavering.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.22: Endowed with that faith, that devotee worships that deity and obtains the desired objects from it — which are in fact granted by Me alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.23: But that fruit of those small-minded ones is finite (antavat). Those who worship the gods go to the gods; My devotees come to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.24: The unintelligent (abuddhayaḥ) think that I, the Unmanifest, have come into manifestation. They do not know My supreme, imperishable, unsurpassed nature.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.25: Veiled by My yoga-māyā, I am not manifest to all. This deluded world does not know Me — the unborn (aja), the imperishable (avyaya).

Bhagavad Gītā 7.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.26: O Arjuna, I know all beings — past, present, and future — but no one knows Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.27: O Bhārata, O Parantapa, all beings fall into complete delusion at birth through the delusion of the pairs of opposites (dvandva-moha) arising from desire and aversion.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.28: But those persons of virtuous deeds whose sin has come to an end — freed from the delusion of pairs of opposites, they worship Me with unwavering resolve (dṛḍha-vratāḥ).

Bhagavad Gītā 7.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.29: Those who strive for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me — they know that Brahman in full, the adhyātman, and all about karma.

Bhagavad Gītā 7.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.30: Those who know Me together with adhibhūta (the material domain), adhidaiva (the divine domain), and adhiyajña (the domain of sacrifice) — those of integrated consciousness (yukta-cetasaḥ) know Me even at the time of death (prayāṇa-kāle).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.1: Arjuna said: O Puruṣottama (best among men), what is that Brahman? What is adhyātman? What is karma? What is said to be adhibhūta? And what is adhidaiva called?

Bhagavad Gītā 8.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.2: O Madhusūdana, who is adhiyajña here, and how does it reside in this body? And how are You to be known at the time of departure (prayāṇa-kāle) by those of steadfast self (niyatātmabhiḥ)?

Bhagavad Gītā 8.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.3: The Blessed Lord said: The Supreme Imperishable (akṣara) is Brahman; one's own essential nature (svabhāva) is called adhyātman; and the creative offering (visarga) that brings forth the existence of beings is called karma.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.4: Adhibhūta is the perishable (kṣara) nature of beings; the cosmic Puruṣa (Hiraṇyagarbha) is adhidaivata; and O best among the embodied, I myself am the adhiyajña here in this body.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.5: And whoever, at the time of death, departs remembering Me alone, leaving the body — that person attains My state (mad-bhāvaṃ). Of this there is no doubt.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.6: O Kaunteya, whatever state of being one remembers when one finally leaves the body — that state alone is reached, always having been absorbed in that very state of being.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.7: Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight. With mind and intellect surrendered to Me (mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ), you shall come to Me alone — without doubt.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.8: O Pārtha, one who meditates continuously with a mind made steadfast through the yoga of practice (abhyāsa-yoga), not wandering to anything else — that person reaches the Supreme Divine Puruṣa.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.9: Whoever meditates on the Seer (kavi), the Ancient (purāṇa), the Ruler (anuśāsitāram), subtler than the atom (aṇor aṇīyāṃsam), the Sustainer of all (sarvasya dhātāram), of inconceivable form (acintya-rūpam), luminous as the sun (āditya-varṇam), beyond all darkness —

Bhagavad Gītā 8.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.10: At the time of departure, with steady mind, endowed with devotion and the power of yoga, fixing the prāṇa (vital force) rightly between the eyebrows — that person reaches that Supreme Divine Puruṣa.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.11: That which the knowers of the Vedas call the Imperishable (akṣaram), which the passion-free ascetics enter, desiring which they practice celibacy (brahmacarya) — that goal I will declare to you briefly.
