Bhagavad Gītā 8.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.12: Having restrained all the gates of the body (sense-organs), having confined the mind in the heart, having placed the prāṇa in the head, established in yogic concentration (yoga-dhāraṇā) —

Bhagavad Gītā 8.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.13: Uttering Om — the single-syllable Brahman — and remembering Me, whoever departs leaving the body — that person attains the supreme destination (paramāṃ gatim).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.14: O Pārtha, for one who continuously and constantly remembers Me with an undivided mind (ananya-cetāḥ) — for that ever-united yogī, I am easily attained (sulabhaḥ).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.15: Having attained Me, those great souls (mahātmānaḥ) who have reached the highest perfection do not take birth again in this transient abode of suffering (duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.16: O Arjuna, all the worlds — up to and including the realm of Brahmā (Brahmaloka) — are subject to return (punar āvartinaḥ). But O Kaunteya, having reached Me, rebirth does not occur.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.17: Those who know that the day of Brahmā extends to a thousand yugas, and that the night of Brahmā also extends to a thousand yugas — they know the reality of day and night.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.18: At the coming of Brahmā's day, all manifest beings arise from the Unmanifest (avyakta); at the coming of night, they dissolve into that same Unmanifest.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.19: O Pārtha, this same multitude of beings (bhūta-grāmaḥ), arising again and again, dissolves helplessly (avaśaḥ) at the coming of night and rises again at the coming of day.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.20: But beyond that Unmanifest, there is yet another eternal Unmanifest — which does not perish even when all beings perish.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.21: That which is called the Unmanifest, the Imperishable (akṣara) — that they call the supreme destination (paramāṃ gatim). That which, having attained, none return — that is My supreme abode (tad dhāma paramaṃ mama).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.22: O Pārtha, that Supreme Puruṣa is attained through undivided devotion (ananyā bhakti) — in whom all beings abide, and by whom all this is pervaded.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.23: O best of the Bharatas, I will describe the times (paths) in which yogīs departing attain non-return (anāvṛttim — liberation) and return (āvṛttim — rebirth).

Bhagavad Gītā 8.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.24: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight (śukla-pakṣa), and the six months of the northern solstice (uttarāyaṇa) — departing in these, the knowers of Brahman (brahma-vidaḥ) go to Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.25: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇa-pakṣa), and the six months of the southern solstice (dakṣiṇāyana) — in these, the yogī reaches the lunar light (cāndramasaṃ jyotir) and returns.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.26: These two paths — the bright (śukla) and the dark (kṛṣṇa) — are considered eternal (śāśvate) for the world. By one, non-return (liberation) is attained; by the other, one returns again.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.27: O Pārtha, knowing these two paths, no yogī is deluded. Therefore, O Arjuna, be yoga-yukta (united with yoga) at all times.

Bhagavad Gītā 8.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.28: Whatever meritorious fruits have been declared for the study of the Vedas, for sacrifices, for austerities, and for charitable gifts — the yogī who knows all this transcends all of these and attains the supreme, primordial abode (paraṃ sthānam ādyam).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.1: The Blessed Lord said: To you who are free from envy, I shall now fully declare this most secret knowledge combined with direct realization, knowing which you shall be liberated from all that is inauspicious.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.2: This is the sovereign knowledge, the sovereign secret, the supreme purifier; directly perceptible, in accordance with dharma, very easy to practice, and imperishable.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.3: O scorcher of foes, those persons who have no faith in this dharma, not attaining Me, return to the path of death and rebirth.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.4: By Me, in My unmanifest form, this entire universe is pervaded. All beings exist in Me, yet I am not contained within them.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.5: Nor do beings rest in Me — behold My divine mystery (yoga)! My Self, which brings forth and sustains all beings, does not dwell within them.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.6: Just as the mighty wind, moving everywhere, eternally abides in space (ākāśa), so understand that all beings abide in Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.7: O son of Kunti, all beings merge into My nature at the end of a kalpa (cosmic cycle), and at the beginning of the next kalpa, I send them forth again.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.8: Presiding over My own nature, I project forth again and again this entire multitude of beings, which are helpless, being subject to the force of nature (prakṛti).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.9: And these actions do not bind Me, O Dhanañjaya, for I remain seated as one indifferent (udāsīnavat), unattached to those actions.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.10: Under My superintendence, O Kaunteya, Nature (prakṛti) brings forth the moving and the unmoving. By this reason the world revolves (is constantly in flux).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.11: Fools disregard Me when I dwell in a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.12: Those of bewildered mind take refuge in the deluding nature of demons and fiends — their hopes are vain, their actions vain, their knowledge vain.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.13: But O Pārtha, great souls (mahātmās), sheltered in the divine nature, worship Me with undivided mind, knowing Me as the imperishable origin of all beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.14: Always singing My glories, striving with firm resolve, bowing before Me with devotion — these ever-steadfast ones worship Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.15: And others, worshipping through the sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña), worship Me as the One, as the Distinct, and in many forms facing all directions.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.16: I am the ritual (kratu), I am the sacrifice (yajña), I am the oblation to ancestors (svadhā), I am the medicinal herb (auṣadha), I am the sacred mantra, I am the clarified butter (ājya), I am the sacred fire, and I am the act of offering.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.17: I am the father of this universe, the mother, the sustainer, the grandsire; I am the knowable (vedyam), the purifier, the syllable Oṃ; and I am the Ṛg, the Sāma, and the Yajur Veda.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.18: I am the goal, the sustainer, the Lord, the witness, the abode, the refuge, the selfless friend; I am origin and dissolution, the foundation, the resting place, and the imperishable seed.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.19: I give heat; I withhold and I send forth the rain; I am immortality and also death; I am both being (sat) and non-being (asat), O Arjuna.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.20: The knowers of the three Vedas, who drink the soma and are purified of sin, worship Me through sacrifices, praying for passage to heaven. They reach the holy realm of Indra and enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods in heaven.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.21: Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world, when their merit is exhausted, they re-enter the mortal world. Thus, following the dharma of the three Vedas, those who desire enjoyment attain only the cycle of coming and going.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.22: For those persons who worship Me with undivided devotion, meditating on My transcendental form — to those ever-steadfast ones I personally carry what they lack and preserve what they have (yoga-kṣemam).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.23: O Kaunteya, even those devotees who, endowed with faith, worship other gods — they too worship Me alone, but in an improper (unregulated) manner.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.24: For I am the only enjoyer and the only Lord of all sacrifices. Those who do not know Me in truth fall down (from their attainment).

Bhagavad Gītā 9.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.25: Worshippers of the gods go to the gods; those devoted to ancestors reach the ancestors; those who worship spirits go to the spirits; and those who worship Me come to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.26: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water — that offering of love from the pure-hearted one I accept.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.27: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give in charity, whatever austerity you practice — O Kaunteya, do that as an offering to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.28: Thus you shall be liberated from the bondage of actions with their good and evil results. With the spirit disciplined in the yoga of renunciation (sannyāsa-yoga), you shall become free and come to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.29: I am equal toward all beings; none is hateful to Me and none is dear. Yet those who worship Me with devotion are in Me, and I am also in them.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.30: Even if a person of very evil conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, he must be regarded as righteous (sādhu), for he has resolved rightly.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.31: He swiftly becomes a righteous soul and attains everlasting peace. O Kaunteya, declare with certainty: My devotee is never lost.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.32: O Pārtha, even those who may be born of sinful wombs — women, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras — even they, taking refuge in Me, attain the supreme destination.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.33: How much more, then, the pure Brāhmaṇas and the devoted royal sages! Having obtained this transient and joyless world, worship Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 9.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 9.34: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me, bow down to Me. Having thus disciplined yourself, with Me as your supreme goal, you shall come to Me alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.1: The Blessed Lord said: O mighty-armed, hear once more My supreme word, which I shall speak to you with love, desiring your welfare.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.2: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know My origin, for I am in every way the ultimate source (ādi) of the gods and great sages.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.3: He who knows Me as unborn (aja), without beginning (anādi), and the great Lord of all worlds — among mortals, he is undeluded, and is freed from all sins.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.4: Intelligence, knowledge, freedom from delusion, patience, truth, self-restraint of the senses, calmness of mind, pleasure, pain, birth, death, fear, and fearlessness —

Bhagavad Gītā 10.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.5: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and infamy — these diverse states of beings all arise from Me alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.6: The seven great sages of old, and the four (Sanaka and his brothers) before them, and the Manus — born from My mind, imbued with My power — from them come all the creatures of the world.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.7: He who knows, in truth, this My divine glory (vibhūti) and power (yoga) — he becomes united with Me through unwavering yoga. Of this there is no doubt.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.8: I am the source of all; everything proceeds from Me. Knowing this, the wise, endowed with true feeling, worship Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.9: With their minds fixed on Me, with their life-breath offered to Me, enlightening each other, and always speaking of Me, they are ever contented and delighted.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.10: To those who are ever devoted, who worship Me with love — I give that yoga of intelligence (buddhi-yoga) by which they come to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.11: Out of compassion for them alone, dwelling within their very being, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the brilliant lamp of knowledge.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.12: Arjuna said: You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode (dhāma), the supreme purifier. You are the eternal, divine Puruṣa, the primordial God (ādideva), unborn and all-pervading (vibhu).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.13: All the sages declare this of You — the divine sage Nārada, Asita, Devala, and Vyāsa — and You Yourself tell me so.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.14: All this that You tell me, O Keśava, I hold to be true. O Lord (Bhagavan), neither the gods nor the demons know Your true manifestation.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.15: You alone know Yourself by Yourself, O Puruṣottama, O source of beings (Bhūtabhāvana), O Lord of beings (Bhūteśa), O God of gods (Devadeva), O Lord of the universe (Jagatpate).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.16: You alone are worthy of fully declaring Your own divine glories (vibhūtis) — by which manifestations You pervade and stand in these worlds.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.17: O Yogin, O Lord, how may I know You, always meditating? And in which particular forms (bhāvas) are You to be contemplated by me?

Bhagavad Gītā 10.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.18: Tell me again in full, O Janārdana, of Your yoga-power and divine glories — for in listening to this nectar (amṛtam), I am never satisfied.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.19: The Blessed Lord said: Very well! I shall tell you of My divine glories, O best of the Kurus — but only the principal ones, for there is no end to My extent.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.20: O Guḍākeśa (conqueror of sleep), I am the Self (ātman) dwelling in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.21: Among the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; among lights, the radiant sun; among the Maruts I am Marīci; among the stars I am the moon.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.22: Among the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; among the gods I am Vāsava (Indra); among the senses I am the mind; and among beings I am consciousness (cetanā).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.23: Among the Rudras I am Śaṅkara (Śiva); among the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas I am Kubera (Vitteśa, lord of wealth); among the Vasus I am Pāvaka (fire); and among mountains I am Meru.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.24: O Pārtha, know Me as Bṛhaspati, the chief among priests; among generals I am Skanda; among bodies of water I am the ocean.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.25: Among the great sages I am Bhṛgu; among words I am the single syllable Oṃ; among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition (japa-yajña); and among immovable things I am the Himālaya.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.26: Among all trees I am the aśvattha (peepal/sacred fig); among the divine sages I am Nārada; among the Gandharvas I am Citraratha; among the Siddhas I am the sage Kapila.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.27: Among horses know Me as Uccaiḥśravas, born of the nectar-churning; among the lordly elephants, Airāvata; and among men, the king.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.28: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt (vajra); among cows, the wish-fulfilling cow (Kāmadhuk); among progenitors I am Kandarpa (Kāmadeva, god of love); among serpents I am Vāsuki.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.29: Among the Nāgas I am Ananta (Śeṣa); among aquatic beings I am Varuṇa; among the ancestors I am Aryamā; among those who maintain order I am Yama.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.30: Among the Daityas I am Prahlāda; among reckoners I am Time (Kāla); among beasts I am the lion (king of animals); and among birds I am Vainateyā (Garuḍa).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.31: Among purifiers I am the wind (Pavana); among weapon-bearers I am Rāma; among fish I am the Makara (crocodile/sea-monster); and among rivers I am the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.32: O Arjuna, I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all creations. Among all knowledge-systems I am the science of the Self (adhyātma-vidyā); and among those who reason and debate, I am the truth-seeking argument (vāda).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.33: Among letters I am the letter 'A'; among grammatical compounds I am the dvandva (copulative compound). I am imperishable Time itself, and I am the Creator facing in all directions (viśvatomukha).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.34: I am death that seizes all, and I am the origin of those yet to be born. Among the feminine virtues, I am Fame (Kīrti), Prosperity (Śrī), Speech (Vāk), Memory (Smṛti), Intelligence (Medhā), Steadfastness (Dhṛti), and Forbearance (Kṣamā).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.35.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.35: Among the Sāma hymns I am the Bṛhatsāma; among poetic meters I am the Gāyatrī; among months I am Mārgaśīrṣa (November–December); and among seasons I am the flower-bearing spring (Kusumākara).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.36.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.36: Among the deceitful I am gambling (dyūta); I am the splendor of the splendorous; I am victory; I am resolute effort (vyavasāya); and I am the goodness (sattva) of the good.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.37.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.37: Among the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva (Krishna Himself); among the Pāṇḍavas I am Dhanañjaya (Arjuna); among sages I am Vyāsa; and among poets I am Uśanā (Śukrācārya).

Bhagavad Gītā 10.38.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.38: Among those who punish and subdue, I am the Rod of Chastisement (Daṇḍa); among those who seek to win, I am statecraft (Nīti); among secrets I am Silence (Mauna); and I am the knowledge of those who know.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.39.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.39: And whatever is the seed-cause of all beings, O Arjuna, that too am I. There is no being — moving or unmoving — that can exist without Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.40.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.40: O Parantapa, there is no end to My divine manifestations. What I have declared is only an indicative enumeration (uddeśataḥ) — a sample — of My infinite glory.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.41.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.41: Whatever being is endowed with glory (vibhūtimat), or is prosperous (śrīmat), or is powerfully vigorous (ūrjitam) — know that every such being arises from but a spark of My splendor.

Bhagavad Gītā 10.42.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.42: Or rather, O Arjuna, what is the use of this much detailed knowledge for you? I pervade and sustain this entire universe with but a single fraction (ekāṃśena) of Myself — and yet remain.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.1: Arjuna said: In order to show grace to me, You have declared the supreme secret known as adhyātma (the knowledge of the Self). Through those words of Yours, this delusion of mine has been dispelled.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.2: O Lotus-eyed One, I have heard in detail from You about the origin and dissolution of all beings, and also Your inexhaustible greatness.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.3: O Supreme Lord, what You have spoken about Yourself is exactly so — I accept it as truth. Yet, O Puruṣottama, I wish to see Your lordly form (aiśvara-rūpa) directly.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.4: O Lord, if You think it possible for me to see it — then O Yogeśvara (Lord of Yoga), reveal to me Your imperishable Self.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.5: The Blessed Lord said: O Pārtha, behold My forms — hundreds and thousands of them, of many kinds, divine, of many colors and shapes.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.6: Behold the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Aśvins, and the Maruts — behold the many wonders, O Bhārata, never seen before.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.7: O Guḍākeśa (conqueror of sleep), behold now, here in My body, the entire universe — moving and unmoving — gathered in one place, and whatever else you wish to see.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.8: But you are not able to see Me with these ordinary eyes of yours. I grant you a divine eye. Behold My lordly Yoga (supreme power).

Bhagavad Gītā 11.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.9: Sañjaya said: O King, having spoken thus, the great Lord of all Yoga — Hari — revealed to Pārtha His supreme and lordly form.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.10: With many mouths and eyes, with many wondrous aspects to behold, with many divine ornaments, with many divine weapons upraised —

Bhagavad Gītā 11.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.11: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances — all-wondrous, infinite, facing in all directions — that Divine Being —

Bhagavad Gītā 11.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.12: If a thousand suns were to blaze forth simultaneously in the sky — that radiance might approach the radiance of that Great Being.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.13: Then, in the body of the God of gods, Pāṇḍava (Arjuna) saw the entire universe — unified in one place, yet divided in many ways.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.14: Then, overwhelmed with wonder, with hair standing on end, Dhanañjaya bowed his head before the Divine, and with palms joined, spoke.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.15: Arjuna said: O Lord, in Your body I see all the gods and also the hosts of all kinds of beings — Brahmā seated on the lotus, Śiva (Lord of all), all the sages, and the divine serpents.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.16: I behold You everywhere — infinite in form, with countless arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes. O Lord of the Universe, O Universal Form, I see no end, no middle, and no beginning of You.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.17: I behold You with crown, mace, and discus — a mass of radiance blazing everywhere, difficult to look at, shining like blazing fire and the sun, immeasurable.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.18: You are the imperishable Supreme, the highest to be known, the ultimate repository of this universe. You are the undecaying guardian of eternal dharma. I regard You as the primeval, everlasting Puruṣa.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.19: Without beginning, middle, or end, of infinite valor, with endless arms, with the moon and sun as Your eyes, I see You — with blazing fire-mouths, warming this entire universe with Your own radiance.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.20: O Great Being, the entire space between heaven and earth and all the directions are pervaded by You alone. The three worlds tremble with fear upon beholding this wondrous and terrible form of Yours.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.21: These hosts of gods are entering into You; some, struck with fear, praise You with joined palms; the great sages and perfected ones (siddhas) cry 'May it be auspicious!' and praise You with magnificent hymns.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.22: The Rudras, Ādityas, Vasus, Sādhyas, Viśvedevas, the two Aśvins, the Maruts, the Uṣmapas (ancestral beings), Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, and the hosts of Siddhas — all behold You in astonishment.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.23: O Mighty-armed One, beholding Your vast form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet, many bellies, and many terrible tusks — the worlds are terrified, and so am I.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.24: Beholding You touching the sky, blazing, many-colored, with gaping mouths, with huge flaming eyes — my inner self is terrified, O Viṣṇu, and I find neither courage nor peace.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.25: Beholding Your mouths — terrible with fangs, like the fires of cosmic dissolution — I lose all sense of direction and find no comfort. Be gracious, O Lord of Gods, O Abode of the Universe.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.26: All these sons of Dhritarashtra, together with the hosts of kings — Bhishma, Drona, and that son of a charioteer (Karna), and also the chief warriors of our own side — all are entering into You.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.27: Rushing swiftly, they enter Your terrible mouths armed with fearful tusks. Some are seen dangling between Your teeth with their heads crushed to powder.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.28: As the many rushing torrents of rivers flow irresistibly toward the ocean, so these heroes of the human world enter into Your blazing mouths.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.29: As moths rush with great speed into a blazing fire for their own destruction, so too do these creatures rush into Your mouths with great speed for their destruction.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.30: O Viṣṇu! Licking all the worlds from every side with Your blazing mouths, You devour them. Your fierce radiances fill the entire universe, scorching it with their brilliance.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.31: Tell me — who are You in this fierce form? My salutations to You, O best among gods; be gracious. I wish to know You, the Primordial — for I do not comprehend Your activity (pravṛtti).

Bhagavad Gītā 11.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.32: The Blessed Lord said: I am mighty, world-destroying Time (Kāla), now fully manifested here to annihilate these worlds. Even without you, all the warriors arrayed in the opposing armies shall cease to exist.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.33: Therefore, arise! Win glory! Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. These warriors have already been slain by Me long before — be only the instrument, O Savyasācin (Arjuna, the ambidextrous archer).

Bhagavad Gītā 11.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.34: Drona, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa, and the other great warrior-heroes — already slain by Me — do you slay them. Be not distressed. Fight! You shall conquer your enemies in battle.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.35.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.35: Sañjaya said: Having heard this utterance of Keśava, the crowned one (Kirīṭī, Arjuna) — trembling, hands folded in reverence — bowed to Kṛṣṇa, and once more prostrating himself in great fear, spoke with a voice choked with emotion —

Bhagavad Gītā 11.36.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.36: Arjuna said: O Hṛṣīkeśa (master of the senses), it is right and fitting that the world is delighted and becomes deeply enamored at the singing of Your glory. The rākṣasas, terror-stricken, flee in all directions, while all the assemblies of siddhas (perfected beings) bow to You.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.37.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.37: O great soul (Mahātman), why should they not bow to You — who are greater even than Brahmā, the original creator? O Infinite (Ananta)! O Lord of the gods (Deveśa)! O Abode of the universe (Jagannivāsa)! You are that imperishable (Akṣara) which is beyond both sat (being) and asat (non-being) — that supreme Reality.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.38.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.38: You are the first God (Ādideva), the ancient Person (Purāṇa-Puruṣa); You are the supreme resting place (paraṃ nidhānam) of this universe. You are the Knower, the Knowable, and the Supreme Abode. O Infinite-formed (Ananta-rūpa), by You is this universe pervaded.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.39.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.39: You are Vāyu (wind), Yama (death), Agni (fire), Varuṇa (water), Śaśāṅka (moon), Prajāpati (Brahmā), and even the father of Brahmā (prapitāmaha). Salutation to You! Salutation a thousand times! And again — salutation upon salutation to You!

Bhagavad Gītā 11.40.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.40: Salutation from the front and from behind! O All (Sarva), salutation from every side! O You of infinite valor and boundless might — You pervade everything, and therefore You are everything.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.41.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.41: Whatever I have said rashly — treating You as a friend, without knowing this greatness of Yours — 'O Kṛṣṇa! O Yādava! O my friend!' — whether from carelessness or from love —

Bhagavad Gītā 11.42.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.42: During our sports, our resting, our sitting, and our meals — alone or even in the presence of others — O Acyuta (the unfaltering)! — for whatever disrespect was shown through jesting or insult, I ask forgiveness of You, the Immeasurable (Aprameyam).

Bhagavad Gītā 11.43.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.43: You are the Father of the world — of all that moves and is unmoving. You are the most venerable and the greatest Guru. In the three worlds there is none equal to You — then how could there be one greater, O You of incomparable glory (Apratimaprabhāva)?

Bhagavad Gītā 11.44.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.44: Therefore, laying my body down in prostration, I entreat You — the adorable Lord — for Your grace. O God, just as a father bears with his son, a friend with his friend, and a lover with a beloved — so You must bear with me.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.45.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.45: Having seen what has never been seen before, I am exhilarated — and yet my mind is overwhelmed with fear. Show me that form of Yours as the Deva (the gentle divine form), O Lord of Gods (Deveśa), O Abode of the Universe (Jagannivāsa)! Be gracious.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.46.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.46: O Thousand-armed (Sahasrabāho), O Cosmic Form (Viśvamūrte) — I wish to see You just as You were before: with the crown (kirīṭa), holding the mace (gadā), with the discus (cakra) in hand. Please appear in that four-armed form.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.48.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.48: O best of the Kurus (Kurupravīra), this form of Mine cannot be seen in the human world by anyone other than you — not through study of the Vedas, not through sacrifice, not through charity, not through ritual acts, and not through fierce austerities.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.49.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.49: Do not be distressed, and do not be bewildered, having seen this terrible form of Mine. Free from fear, with a gladdened heart — see once again this (gentle) form of Mine.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.50.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.50: Sañjaya said: Having thus spoken to Arjuna, Vāsudeva revealed His own (gentle) form once again. The great soul (Mahātmā), reassuming His gentle human form, reassured the frightened Arjuna.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.47.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.47: The Blessed Lord said: O Arjuna, by My grace and through My own divine power (ātmayogāt), I have shown you this supreme, luminous, universal, infinite, and primordial Form — which has never been seen before by anyone other than you.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.51.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.51: Arjuna said: O Janārdana, seeing this gentle human form of Yours, I have now regained my composure and am returned to my own natural state (prakṛtim gataḥ).

Bhagavad Gītā 11.52.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.52: The Blessed Lord said: This form of Mine that you have seen is extremely difficult to behold. Even the gods eternally long for the vision of this form.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.53.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.53: Not through the Vedas, not through austerity, not through charity, and not through sacrifice can I be seen in this manner as you have seen Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.54.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.54: But O Parantapa (Arjuna), by undivided devotion (ananyayā bhaktyā) alone can I be known in truth, seen thus, and entered into.

Bhagavad Gītā 11.55.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.55: O Pāṇḍava, one who performs actions for My sake, who regards Me as the Supreme, who is devoted to Me, who is free from attachment, and who is free from enmity toward all beings — such a one attains Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 12.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.1: Arjuna said: Those devotees who are ever steadfast and worship You thus — and those who worship the Imperishable, the Unmanifest (akṣaram avyaktam) — which of these know yoga better?

Bhagavad Gītā 12.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.2: The Blessed Lord said: Those who, fixing their mind on Me, worship Me, ever steadfast and endowed with supreme faith (śraddhayā parayā) — they, in My view, are the most united (yuktatamāḥ).

Bhagavad Gītā 12.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.3: But those who worship the Imperishable (akṣara), the Undefinable (anirdeśyam), the Unmanifest, the Omnipresent, the Inconceivable, the Immutable (kūṭa-stha), the Immovable, the Constant —

Bhagavad Gītā 12.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.4: Having thoroughly restrained all the senses, even-minded everywhere (sama-buddhayaḥ), devoted to the welfare of all beings (sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ) — they also reach Me alone.

Bhagavad Gītā 12.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.5: For those whose minds are attached to the Unmanifest, the difficulty (kleśa) is far greater; for the way of the Unmanifest is attained with difficulty by embodied beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 12.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.6: But those who, having surrendered all actions to Me, holding Me as the Supreme, worship Me, meditating on Me with undivided yoga (ananyena yogena) —

Bhagavad Gītā 12.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.7: O Pārtha, for those whose consciousness is absorbed in Me (mayy āveśita-cetasām), I become their swift deliverer (samuddhartā) from the ocean of death-bound existence (mṛtyu-saṃsāra-sāgarāt).

Bhagavad Gītā 12.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.8: Fix your mind on Me alone; place your intellect in Me. Hereafter you shall dwell in Me alone — of this there is no doubt.

Bhagavad Gītā 12.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.9: O Dhanañjaya, if you are unable to hold the mind steady in Me, then seek to attain Me through the yoga of practice (abhyāsa-yoga).

Bhagavad Gītā 12.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.10: If you are even incapable of practice (abhyāsa), then be devoted to performing actions for My sake. Even performing actions for My sake, you shall attain perfection (siddhi).

Bhagavad Gītā 12.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.11: If you are unable to do even this, then, taking refuge in My yoga, with a controlled self (yatātmavān), renounce the fruits of all actions.

Bhagavad Gītā 12.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.12: Knowledge is better than practice (abhyāsa); meditation is superior to knowledge; renunciation of the fruits of action (karma-phala-tyāga) is superior to meditation; and from renunciation, peace follows immediately (anantaram).

Bhagavad Gītā 12.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.13: One who harbors no hatred toward any being (adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānām), who is friendly (maitraḥ) and compassionate (karuṇaḥ), free from the sense of 'mine' (nirmamaḥ), free from ego (nirahaṃkāraḥ), equanimous in pain and pleasure (sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ), and forgiving (kṣamī) —

Bhagavad Gītā 12.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.14: Who is always content, a yogī, self-controlled (yatātmā), of firm conviction (dṛḍha-niścayaḥ), with mind and intellect offered to Me — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me (sa me priyaḥ).

Bhagavad Gītā 12.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.15: One from whom the world is not distressed, and who is not distressed by the world; who is free from joy, envy, fear, and agitation (harṣāmarṣa-bhayodvegaiḥ) — that one is also dear to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 12.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.16: One who is without expectation (anapekṣaḥ), pure (śuciḥ), capable (dakṣaḥ), impartial (udāsīnaḥ), free from anguish (gata-vyathaḥ), who has abandoned all ego-driven undertakings (sarvārambha-parityāgī) — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 12.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.17: One who neither rejoices (na hṛṣyati) nor hates, neither grieves nor desires; who has renounced both the auspicious and the inauspicious — that devotee, full of bhakti (bhaktimān), is dear to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 12.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.18: One who is equal to enemy and friend, equal in honor and dishonor; equal in cold, heat, pleasure and pain; free from attachment (saṅga-vivarjitaḥ) —

Bhagavad Gītā 12.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.19: Equal in praise and blame (tulya-nindā-stutiḥ), silent (maunī), content with whatever comes (santuṣṭo yena kenacit), homeless (aniketaḥ), of steady mind (sthira-matiḥ), full of devotion — that person is dear to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 12.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 12.20: But those who with faith (śraddadhānāḥ), holding Me as the Supreme (mat-paramāḥ), worship this dharmic nectar (dharmyāmṛtam) as expounded — those devotees are exceedingly (atīva) dear to Me.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.1: Arjuna said: O Keśava, I wish to know Prakṛti and Puruṣa, the Field and the Knower of the Field, and Knowledge and the Object of Knowledge. The Blessed Lord said: O son of Kuntī, this body is called the 'Field' (kṣetra). Those who know this say that the one who knows it is the 'Knower of the Field' (kṣetrajña).

Bhagavad Gītā 13.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.2: O Bhārata, know Me also as the Kṣetrajña in all fields. The knowledge of the field and the knower of the field — that, in My view, is (true) knowledge.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.3: Hear from Me in brief — what the kṣetra is and of what nature; what its modifications are, from what it arose; who that one (kṣetrajña) is, and what his power (prabhāva).

Bhagavad Gītā 13.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.4: This has been sung by the seers in many ways, separately in various hymns (chandas), and also in the reasoned and conclusive passages of the Brahma-sūtra.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.5: The five great elements, ego (ahaṃkāra), intellect (buddhi), and the unmanifest (avyakta); the ten senses and one (mind); and the five sense-objects —

Bhagavad Gītā 13.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.6: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate (body-complex), consciousness, and steadiness — this, with its modifications, is the kṣetra (field) described briefly.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.7: Absence of pride (amānitva), absence of pretension (adambhitva), non-violence (ahiṃsā), patience (kṣānti), uprightness (ārjava), service to the teacher (ācāryopāsana), cleanliness (śauca), steadiness (sthairya), self-restraint (ātma-vinigraha) —

Bhagavad Gītā 13.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.8: Dispassion toward sense-objects (vairāgya); freedom from ego (anahaṃkāra); and the continuous perception of the evil inherent in birth, death, old age, disease, sorrow, and fault —

Bhagavad Gītā 13.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.9: Non-attachment (asakti) and non-clinging (anabhiṣvaṅga) to son, wife, home, and so on; and constant evenness of mind in the arising of the desirable and the undesirable —

Bhagavad Gītā 13.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.10: Unwavering devotion to Me through exclusive yoga (ananya-yoga); resorting to solitary places; and distaste for the company of crowds —

Bhagavad Gītā 13.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.11: Constancy in self-knowledge (adhyātma-jñāna-nityatva) and the perception of the purpose of true knowledge (tattva-jñānārtha-darśana) — this is declared to be knowledge (jñāna). What is contrary to this is ignorance (ajñāna).

Bhagavad Gītā 13.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.12: I will declare that which is to be known (jñeyam) — by knowing which, one attains immortality (amṛta). It is the beginningless Supreme Brahman — it is said to be neither existent (sat) nor non-existent (asat).

Bhagavad Gītā 13.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.13: With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere, with ears everywhere — it abides in the world, encompassing all.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.14: Illuminating the functions of all senses, yet without any senses; unattached yet the supporter of all; devoid of qualities (nirguṇa), yet the experiencer of qualities —

Bhagavad Gītā 13.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.15: That Knowable (Brahman) is outside and inside all beings, the unmoving and the moving alike. Because of its subtlety it is incomprehensible. It is far away, and yet it is near.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.16: That Knowable appears as divided among beings yet remains undivided. It is the sustainer of all beings, and it is the devourer and the creator.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.17: That is the Light of lights, said to be beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the Knowable, and the goal of knowledge — established in the heart of all.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.18: Thus the Field, Knowledge, and the Knowable have been described in brief. My devotee, knowing this through direct realization (vijñāna), attains My very being.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.19: Know both Prakṛti and Puruṣa to be beginningless. And know that modifications (vikāras) and the guṇas are born from Prakṛti.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.20: Prakṛti is said to be the cause in the agency of effects and causes. Puruṣa is said to be the cause in the experience of pleasure and pain.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.21: Puruṣa, established in Prakṛti, experiences the guṇas born of Prakṛti. Attachment to the guṇas is the cause of its births in good and evil wombs.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.22: The Supreme Puruṣa in this body is also called the Witness (upadraṣṭā), the Permitter (anumantā), the Sustainer (bhartā), the Experiencer (bhoktā), the Great Lord (maheśvaraḥ), and the Supreme Self (paramātmā).

Bhagavad Gītā 13.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.23: One who knows Puruṣa and Prakṛti together with the guṇas in this way — in whatever way they live — is not born again.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.24: Some behold the Self in the Self by the Self through meditation; others through the yoga of Sāṃkhya; and still others through karma yoga.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.25: But others, not knowing thus, worship having heard from others. Even they cross beyond death — those who are devoted to what they have heard.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.26: O best of the Bharatas, know that whatever being is born — moving or unmoving — arises from the union of the Field and the Knower of the Field.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.27: One who sees the Supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, the imperishable within the perishable — that one truly sees.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.28: Seeing the Lord dwelling equally everywhere, one does not destroy the Self by the self — and thereby attains the supreme goal.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.29: One who sees that all actions are performed in every way by Prakṛti alone, and that the Self is the non-doer — that one truly sees.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.30: When one perceives the separate existence of all beings as resting in the One, and the expansion of all from that same One — then one becomes Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.31: O son of Kuntī, this Supreme Self — being beginningless and beyond the guṇas — is imperishable. Though dwelling in the body, it neither acts nor is tainted.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.32: Just as the all-pervading ether (ākāśa) is not tainted because of its subtlety — so too does the Self, present everywhere in bodies, remain untainted.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.33: O Bhārata, just as the one sun illuminates this entire world — so does the Kṣetrī (the Self, Knower of the Field) illuminate the entire Field.

Bhagavad Gītā 13.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.34: Those who know, through the eye of knowledge, the distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field — and liberation from the Prakṛti of beings — they attain the Supreme.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.1: Śrī Bhagavān said: I shall declare once more the supreme knowledge — the highest of all knowledges — knowing which all the sages have gone from this world to the highest perfection.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.2: Taking refuge in this knowledge and attaining identity with my own nature, they are neither born at creation nor disturbed at dissolution.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.3: My womb is the great Brahma (Mahā Prakṛti); in that I place the embryo. From that, O Bhārata, is the birth of all beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.4: O Kaunteya, whatever forms are born in all wombs, the Great Brahma (Prakṛti) is their mother-womb, and I am the seed-giving father.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.5: O Mighty-armed, Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas — these Guṇas, born of Prakṛti, bind the imperishable dweller-in-the-body (the Ātman) to the body.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.6: Among these, Sattva, being pure, is illuminating and disease-free, O sinless one; yet it binds through attachment to happiness and attachment to knowledge.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.7: Know that Rajas is passion-natured, born of thirst and attachment; O Kaunteya, it binds the embodied soul through attachment to action.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.8: But know that Tamas is born of ignorance, the deluder of all embodied beings; O Bhārata, it binds through heedlessness, sloth, and sleep.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.9: O Bhārata, Sattva attaches to happiness; Rajas to action; while Tamas, covering knowledge, attaches to heedlessness.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.10: O Bhārata, Sattva arises by suppressing Rajas and Tamas; Rajas by suppressing Sattva and Tamas; and Tamas by suppressing Sattva and Rajas.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.11: When in all the gates of this body, knowledge and light arise — then one should know that Sattva is predominant.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.12: O Best of the Bharatas, when Rajas increases, greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness, and craving arise.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.13: O Joy of the Kurus, when Tamas increases, darkness, inactivity, heedlessness, and delusion arise.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.14: When the embodied one departs when Sattva is predominant, they attain the pure worlds of those who know the highest.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.15: Dying in Rajas, one is born among those attached to action; dying in Tamas, one is born in the wombs of the deluded.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.16: They say the fruit of righteous (Sāttvic) action is pure and flawless; the fruit of Rajas is suffering; and the fruit of Tamas is ignorance.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.17: From Sattva, knowledge arises; from Rajas, greed arises; from Tamas, heedlessness, delusion, and ignorance arise.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.18: Those established in Sattva rise upward; those in Rajas remain in the middle; those in Tamas, established in the lowest Guṇa's functions, go downward.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.19: When the seer perceives no other agent than the Guṇas, and knows what is beyond the Guṇas — he attains my nature.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.20: Having transcended these three Guṇas born of the body, the embodied soul, freed from birth, death, old age, and suffering, attains immortality.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.21: Arjuna said: O Lord, by what marks is one who has transcended these three Guṇas known? What is his conduct? And how does he transcend these three Guṇas?

Bhagavad Gītā 14.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.22: Śrī Bhagavān said: O Pāṇḍava, one who does not resist when illumination (Sattva), activity (Rajas), and delusion (Tamas) arise — and does not crave them when they cease — is said to have transcended the Guṇas.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.23: Seated as one unconcerned (neutral), undisturbed by the Guṇas, knowing that 'the Guṇas alone are functioning' — remaining firm and unshaken — he transcends the Guṇas.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.24: The same in pleasure and pain, self-abiding, seeing a clod of earth, stone, and gold as equal, the same toward the agreeable and disagreeable, steady in mind, equal in blame and self-praise —

Bhagavad Gītā 14.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.25: Equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward friend and foe, renouncing all initiative born of ego — such a one is said to have transcended the Guṇas.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.26: And one who serves Me with unswerving devotion (avyabhicāriṇī bhakti-yoga) — having transcended all these Guṇas — becomes fit for Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 14.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 14.27: For I am the very foundation of Brahman — of the immortal, the imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of absolute bliss.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.1: Śrī Bhagavān said: They speak of an eternal Aśvattha tree with roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns. One who knows this tree is a knower of the Vedas.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.2: Its branches spread both downward and upward, nourished by the three Guṇas, with sense objects as its shoots. And below, in the world of men, its roots extend downward, bound to action.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.3: Its true form is not perceived as such here; neither its end, nor its beginning, nor its real foundation is known. Cutting down this Aśvattha tree with its deep-entrenched roots by the firm sword of non-attachment...

Bhagavad Gītā 15.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.4: ...thereafter that supreme state must be sought, having reached which, none return again. Taking refuge in that very primal Person alone — from whom this ancient flow of creation has streamed forth.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.5: Free from pride and delusion, with the evil of attachment conquered, ever dwelling in the Self, with desires completely extinguished, liberated from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain — the undeluded wise reach that imperishable state.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.6: That which the sun does not illumine, nor the moon, nor fire — that is my supreme abode, reaching which, none return.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.7: An eternal portion of myself, having become the individual soul (jīva) in the world of the living, draws to itself the five senses and the mind as the sixth — all abiding in Prakṛti.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.8: When this lord (the jīva) obtains a body and when it departs from it, it takes these (senses and mind) along with it — just as the wind carries fragrances from their source.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.9: Presiding over the ear, eye, the organ of touch, taste, and smell, as well as the mind — this jīva experiences the sense objects.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.10: The deluded do not perceive this (jīva) as it departs, dwells, or experiences, united with the Guṇas. Those with the eye of knowledge perceive it.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.11: Striving yogīs behold this (jīva) established in the Self. But the unrefined — those of uncultivated inner being — though striving, do not perceive it.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.12: Know that the light in the sun which illumines the entire world, and that which is in the moon, and that which is in fire — know that brilliance to be mine.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.13: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings by my energy; and becoming the Soma (moon), full of rasa (vital essence), I nourish all plants.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.14: Having become Vaiśvānara (the universal digestive fire), dwelling in the bodies of living beings, and united with the prāṇa and apāna vital breaths, I digest the four types of food.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.15: And I am seated in the hearts of all. From me alone come memory, knowledge, and their removal. I alone am to be known by all the Vedas; I am the author of Vedānta and the knower of the Vedas.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.16: Two Puruṣas exist in the world — the perishable (Kṣara) and the imperishable (Akṣara). The Kṣara is all beings; the Kūṭastha (the immovable) is called the Akṣara.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.17: But the Supreme Person is indeed another — spoken of as Paramātman, who, as the imperishable Īśvara, pervades and sustains all three worlds.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.18: Since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable, I am celebrated in the world and in the Veda as Puruṣottama — the Supreme Person.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.19: O Bhārata, one who, without delusion, thus knows me as Puruṣottama — the Supreme Person — knowing all, worships me with his entire being.

Bhagavad Gītā 15.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 15.20: Thus this most secret scripture has been declared by me, O sinless one. Knowing this, O Bhārata, one becomes truly wise and all duties are fulfilled.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.1: Śrī Bhagavān said: Fearlessness, purity of being, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, charity, self-restraint, sacrifice, scriptural study, austerity, and straightforwardness —

Bhagavad Gītā 16.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.2: Non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranquility, absence of calumny, compassion for all beings, freedom from covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and absence of fickleness —

Bhagavad Gītā 16.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.3: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice, and absence of excessive pride — these are the (marks of one) born to the divine endowment, O Bhārata.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.4: O Pārtha, hypocrisy, arrogance, excessive pride, anger, harshness, and ignorance — these are (the marks of one) born to the demoniac endowment.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.5: The divine endowment is considered conducive to liberation, the demoniac to bondage. Do not grieve, O Pāṇḍava — you are born to the divine endowment.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.6: Two kinds of beings are created in this world — the divine and the demoniac. The divine has been described at length. Hear from me about the demoniac, O Pārtha.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.7: The demoniac do not know what to do (pravṛtti) and what to refrain from (nivṛtti). Neither purity, nor right conduct, nor truth is found in them.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.8: They say: the world has no truth, no foundation, no Lord. It arose from mutual union alone — what else? — with desire as its only cause.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.9: Holding fast to this view, these self-ruined ones of stunted intellect arise in this world as enemies of the world, performing terrible deeds for its destruction.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.10: Taking refuge in insatiable desire, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, through delusion grasping at false notions, they move through life with impure resolves.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.11: Beset by immeasurable anxieties lasting until death, holding the gratification of desire as the highest aim, convinced that this alone is all there is —

Bhagavad Gītā 16.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.12: Bound by hundreds of snares of hope, given over to desire and anger, they seek to amass wealth by unjust means for the gratification of their desires.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.13: 'This has today been gained by me; this desire I shall also attain. This wealth is mine, and this too shall be mine again in the future.'

Bhagavad Gītā 16.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.14: 'That enemy has been slain by me, and I shall slay others too. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, powerful and happy.'

Bhagavad Gītā 16.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.15: 'I am wealthy, of noble birth. Who else is equal to me? I shall sacrifice, I shall give, I shall rejoice.' — thus, deluded by ignorance.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.16: Bewildered by many thoughts, enveloped in the net of delusion, deeply addicted to sensual pleasures — they fall into a foul hell.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.17: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride of wealth and honour, they perform sacrifice in name only, with ostentation, disregarding scriptural injunctions.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.18: Taking refuge in egoism, power, arrogance, desire and anger, these malicious persons hate me who dwells in their own and in others' bodies.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.19: These hateful, cruel, vilest among men, these wicked ones — I continuously hurl them into demoniac wombs in the ocean of saṃsāra.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.20: Fallen into demoniac wombs, birth after birth, these deluded ones, O Kaunteya, not attaining Me, sink to the lowest condition from there.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.21: Threefold is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore one should abandon these three.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.22: Released from these three gates of darkness, O Kaunteya, a person practises what is good for the self — and thence attains the supreme goal.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.23: He who, casting aside the injunctions of scripture, acts driven by the impulse of desire — he attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme goal.

Bhagavad Gītā 16.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 16.24: Therefore, let scripture be your authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Knowing what is enjoined by scriptural ordinance, you should perform action here in this world.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.1: Arjuna said: O Kṛṣṇa, what is the condition of those who, setting aside the injunctions of scripture, perform worship with faith — is it sattva, rajas, or tamas?

Bhagavad Gītā 17.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.2: Śrī Bhagavān said: The faith of the embodied beings, born of their inherent nature, is threefold — sāttvika, rājasa, and tāmasa. Hear now of these.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.3: O Bhārata, the faith of every person is in accordance with their inner nature (sattva). This person is made of faith — whatever one's faith is, that indeed one is.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.4: The sāttvika worship the gods; the rājasa worship the yakṣas and rākṣasas; and the others — the tāmasa — worship departed spirits and hosts of lower beings.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.5: Those persons who perform severe austerities not enjoined by scripture — filled with hypocrisy and egoism, impelled by the force of desire and attachment —

Bhagavad Gītā 17.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.6: Torturing the aggregate of elements within the body, and also Me who dwells within the body — know these senseless ones to be of demoniac resolve.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.7: Even the food that is dear to all is of three kinds; and so too are sacrifice, austerity, and charity threefold. Hear now of this distinction.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.8: Foods that promote longevity, vitality, strength, health, happiness, and delight — which are flavourful, smooth, substantial, and pleasing to the heart — are dear to the sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.9: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot, pungent, dry, and burning — these are liked by the rājasika and produce pain, grief, and disease.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.10: Food that is stale, tasteless, putrid, leftover and decayed — and that which is unfit for sacrifice (impure) — is the food dear to the tāmasa.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.11: That sacrifice which is performed according to scriptural ordinance, by those who desire no fruit, with the conviction that 'it is to be performed' and with mind well-focused — that is sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.12: O best of Bhāratas, know that sacrifice which is performed with an eye to its fruit, and also for the sake of ostentation — that sacrifice to be rājasika.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.13: That sacrifice which is contrary to scriptural ordinance, which distributes no food, which lacks mantras, which makes no gifts to priests, and which is devoid of faith — that is declared tāmasika.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.14: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the teachers, and the wise; purity; uprightness; continence; and non-violence — these are said to be the austerity of the body.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.15: Speech that causes no agitation, that is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial — and the practice of scriptural study (svādhyāya) — these are said to be the austerity of speech.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.16: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, and purity of inner disposition — this is declared the austerity of the mind.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.17: That threefold austerity — (physical, verbal, and mental) — which is performed by persons of resolute (yoga), with supreme faith and without expectation of fruit — that is called sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.18: That austerity which is performed for the sake of honour, respect, and worship, and with ostentation — that is here declared rājasika, unstable, and impermanent.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.19: That austerity which is performed with foolish obstinacy, with self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another — that is declared tāmasika.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.20: That gift which is given with the conviction 'it is to be given', to one who cannot repay, in the right place, at the right time, and to a worthy recipient — that gift is remembered as sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.21: But that gift which is given for the sake of a return favour, or again with a view to some fruit, and which is given grudgingly — that gift is remembered as rājasika.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.22: That gift which is given in an inappropriate place and time, to unworthy recipients, without respect, and with contempt — that is declared tāmasika.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.23: 'Oṃ Tat Sat' — this is declared the threefold designation of Brahman. By this were the brāhmaṇas, the Vedas, and the sacrifices ordained of old.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.24: Therefore, the acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity prescribed by ordinance among the followers of Brahman always proceed after uttering 'Oṃ'.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.25: Uttering 'Tat', without aspiration for fruit, the acts of sacrifice and austerity, and the various acts of charity, are performed by those who aspire to liberation.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.26: O Pārtha, 'Sat' is used in the sense of existence-reality and in the sense of goodness; and likewise the word 'Sat' is applied to an auspicious action.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.27: Steadfast commitment in sacrifice, austerity, and charity is also called 'Sat'; and action performed for the sake of these (or for Brahman's sake) is likewise called only 'Sat'.

Bhagavad Gītā 17.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 17.28: O Pārtha, whatever is offered in sacrifice, given in charity, practiced as austerity, or done in any way without faith is called Asat. It yields no result either here or hereafter.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.1.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.1: Arjuna said: O mighty-armed one, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O slayer of Keśī, I wish to know the truth of sannyāsa and tyāga separately.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.2.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.2: Śrī Bhagavān said: The wise understand sannyāsa to be the giving up of desire-motivated actions; the discerning declare tyāga to be the renunciation of the fruits of all actions.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.3.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.3: Some wise thinkers declare that all action is flawed and should be abandoned; while others say that acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should never be abandoned.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.4.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.4: O best of the Bhāratas! O tiger among men! Hear my definitive conclusion regarding renunciation. Renunciation has indeed been declared to be of three kinds.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.5.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.5: Acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should not be abandoned — they must indeed be performed. Sacrifice, charity, and austerity are purifying for the wise.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.6.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.6: But even these actions should be performed, O Pārtha, relinquishing attachment and the fruits. This is my definite and highest conviction.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.7.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.7: The renunciation of one's prescribed duties is not proper. The abandonment of such duties through delusion is declared to be tāmasic renunciation.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.8.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.8: One who abandons an action as painful, out of fear of bodily discomfort, performs a rājasic renunciation and does not obtain the fruit of renunciation.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.9.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.9: But when prescribed action is performed, O Arjuna, simply as duty — having abandoned attachment and fruit — that renunciation is considered sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.10.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.10: The renouncer, saturated with sattva, wise and free from all doubt, does not hate the inauspicious action nor cling to the auspicious.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.11.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.11: For an embodied being it is truly not possible to completely abandon all actions. But one who gives up the fruits of action — that person is truly called a renouncer.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.12.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.12: The threefold fruit of action — the undesirable, the desirable, and the mixed — accrues after death to those who have not relinquished; but never at all to those who have renounced.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.13.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.13: O mighty-armed one, learn from me the five causes that have been stated in Sāṃkhya philosophy for the accomplishment of all actions.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.14.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.14: The seat of action (body), the agent (ego), the various instruments (sense organs), the many different motions (vital functions), and fifth here — fate (daiva) — these are the five causes.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.15.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.15: Whatever action a person undertakes with body, speech, or mind — whether proper or improper — these five are its causes.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.16.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.16: That being so, one who perceives the pure Self alone as the doer — that person, of undeveloped intelligence, is of perverted understanding and does not see truly.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.17.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.17: One whose inner being is free from the sense of 'I am the doer,' whose intelligence is not tainted — even having killed all these worlds, such a person neither kills nor is bound.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.18.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.18: Knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knower — these are the threefold impetus to action (karma-codanā). The instrument, the action, and the agent — these are the threefold basis of action (karma-saṃgraha).

Bhagavad Gītā 18.19.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.19: Knowledge, action, and the agent — these are also of three kinds each, based on the distinction of guṇas, as has been stated in the Sāṃkhya teaching on guṇas. Hear them rightly as well.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.20.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.20: Know that knowledge by which one perceives in all beings a single, imperishable existence — undivided in the divided — to be Sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.21.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.21: But know that knowledge which perceives in all beings separately manifold existences of distinct kinds — through the lens of separateness — to be Rājasa.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.22.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.22: But that knowledge which clings to one single object as if it were everything, which is without rational ground, without grasp of reality, and trivial — that is declared to be Tāmasa.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.23.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.23: Action which is ordained (niyata), free from attachment, performed without passion or aversion, by one who does not desire its fruit — that action is called Sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.24.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.24: But action performed by one who desires objects of enjoyment, or performed again with egoism, and with much exertion — that is declared Rājasa.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.25.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.25: Action that is undertaken out of delusion, without regard for consequences, loss, harm to others, and one's own capacity — that is declared Tāmasa.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.26.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.26: The agent who is free from attachment, who does not claim the doership (non-egotistic), who is endowed with fortitude and enthusiasm, and who is unaffected by success or failure — is called Sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.27.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.27: The agent who is passionate, who craves the fruits of action, who is greedy, of a harmful nature, impure, and who is moved by joy and grief — that agent is declared Rājasa.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.28.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.28: The agent who is undisciplined, vulgar, arrogant, deceitful, malicious toward others, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating — is called Tāmasa.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.29.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.29: Hear now, O Dhanañjaya, the threefold division of intellect (buddhi) and also of fortitude (dhṛti), according to the guṇas — declared in full, distinctly, without remainder.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.30.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.30: O Pārtha, the intellect that knows the paths of engagement (pravṛtti) and withdrawal (nivṛtti), what ought to be done and ought not to be done, what is to be feared and what is not, what is bondage and what is liberation — that intellect is Sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.31.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.31: O Pārtha, the intellect which perceives dharma and adharma, and what ought to be done and what ought not, in a distorted way (not as they truly are) — that intellect is Rājasī.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.32.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.32: O Pārtha, the intellect that, enveloped in darkness (tamas), regards adharma as dharma and sees all things in inverted order — that intellect is Tāmasī.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.33.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.33: O Pārtha, the fortitude (dhṛti) by which — through unwavering yoga — one sustains and directs the activities of the mind, the prāṇa, and the senses — that dhṛti is Sāttvikī.
