Bhagavad Gītā 18.34.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.34: O Pārtha, but the fortitude by which one holds to dharma, kāma (pleasure), and artha (wealth) — with attachment and with desire for the fruit — that dhṛti is Rājasī.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.35.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.35: O Pārtha, the fortitude by which a dull-witted person does not release sleep (sloth), fear, grief, despondency, and arrogance — that dhṛti is Tāmasī.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.36.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.36: O best of Bharatas, hear now from me the threefold nature of pleasure — that in which one rejoices through practice, and which leads to the end of suffering.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.37.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.37: That pleasure which, at first, is like poison, but at the end is like nectar — born of the clarity of one's own Ātman and buddhi — is declared Sāttvika.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.38.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.38: That pleasure arising from the contact of sense organs and sense objects — which at first seems like nectar but at the end is like poison — is remembered as Rājasa.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.39.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.39: That pleasure which — both at the beginning and subsequently — deludes the self, arising from sleep, sloth, and heedlessness — that is declared Tāmasa.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.40.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.40: There is no being on earth, or again in heaven among the gods, that is free from these three guṇas born of Prakṛti.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.43.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.43: Heroism (śaurya), radiant vitality (tejas), steadfast resolve (dhṛti), skill (dākṣya), not fleeing from battle, the quality of generosity (dāna), and the quality of sovereign governance (īśvara-bhāva) — these are the natural duties of a Kṣatriya.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.44.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.44: Agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade are the natural duties of a Vaiśya; and service-oriented action is also the natural duty of a Śūdra.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.45.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.45: Engaged (with deep love and dedication) in one's own duty, a person attains the highest perfection. How one devoted to one's own duty finds this perfection — hear that from me.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.46.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.46: By worshipping through his own duty that Being from whom all creatures have their impulse and by whom all this is pervaded — a man attains perfection.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.47.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.47: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfectly performed, than the dharma of another well-performed. Performing the duty ordained by one's own nature, one incurs no sin.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.48.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.48: O Kaunteya, one should not abandon the duty born of one's own nature, even if it is flawed; for all undertakings are covered by imperfection as fire is covered by smoke.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.49.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.49: One whose intellect is unattached everywhere, whose self is conquered, from whom all longing has departed — through renunciation, that one attains the supreme perfection of non-action (naiṣkarmya).

Bhagavad Gītā 18.50.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.50: O Kaunteya, hear from me briefly how one who has attained perfection reaches Brahman — that is the highest culmination of knowledge.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.51.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.51: Endowed with pure intellect, firmly restraining the self through fortitude, abandoning sound and other objects of the senses, casting aside passion and aversion...

Bhagavad Gītā 18.52.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.52: Resorting to solitude, eating lightly, with speech, body, and mind restrained, ever devoted to dhyāna-yoga, established in dispassion...

Bhagavad Gītā 18.53.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.53: Having relinquished egoism, force, arrogance, desire, anger, and possessiveness — free from the sense of 'mine', at peace — one becomes fit for the realisation of Brahman.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.54.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.54: Having become Brahman, with a serene self, one neither grieves nor desires. Equal toward all beings, one attains the highest devotion to me.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.55.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.55: Through devotion one truly knows me — who I am and what my extent is. Then, having known me in truth, one enters into me immediately thereafter.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.56.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.56: One who takes refuge in me — even while performing all actions always — through my grace attains the eternal, imperishable abode.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.57.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.57: Mentally surrendering all actions to me, regarding me as the supreme goal, taking refuge in the yoga of the intellect — keep your consciousness fixed in me always.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.58.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.58: Being of mind fixed in me, you will cross over all difficulties by my grace. But if, out of ego, you do not listen — you will perish.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.59.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.59: If, taking shelter in ego, you think 'I will not fight' — this resolve of yours is false; your own nature will compel you.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.60.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.60: O Kaunteya, bound by your own action born of your own nature — what you do not wish to do out of delusion — you will do even against your will.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.61.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.61: O Arjuna, the Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, causing all beings to revolve — mounted upon a machine (the body) — by the power of Māyā.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.62.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.62: O Bhārata, take refuge in that very Being with your entire existence. By his grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.63.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.63: Thus this knowledge more secret than all secrets has been declared to you by me. Having reflected on it fully and completely — act as you wish.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.64.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.64: Hear once more my supreme word — the most secret of all. Because you are deeply beloved to me, therefore I shall speak what is beneficial to you.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.65.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.65: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me, bow to me — you will come to me alone. I truly promise you — for you are dear to me.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.66.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.66: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in me alone. I shall liberate you from all sins — do not grieve.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.67.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.67: This is never to be told to one without austerity, nor to one without devotion, nor to one unwilling to listen and serve, nor to one who finds fault with me.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.68.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.68: One who will declare this supreme secret among my devotees — having performed the highest devotion to me — shall come to me alone, without doubt.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.69.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.69: Among human beings, there is none who does what is dearer to me than such a person; nor will there be any other on earth dearer to me than this one.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.70.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.70: And whoever will study this sacred dialogue of ours — by that knowledge-sacrifice (jñāna-yajña) I am worshipped by him: this is my conviction.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.71.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.71: And the person who merely hears this, full of faith and free from malice — even he, liberated from sins, shall attain the auspicious worlds of those who do righteous deeds.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.72.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.72: O Pārtha, has this been heard by you with a one-pointed mind? O Dhanañjaya, has your delusion born of ignorance been completely destroyed?

Bhagavad Gītā 18.73.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.73: Arjuna said: My delusion is destroyed, and I have regained my memory through Your grace, O Infallible One (Acyuta). I stand firm, with my doubts dispelled. I shall do Your word.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.74.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.74: Sañjaya said: Thus have I heard this wondrous, hair-raising dialogue between Vāsudeva and the great-souled Pārtha.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.75.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.75: By the grace of Vyāsa, I have heard this supreme secret, this yoga, directly from Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Yoga, speaking it Himself.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.76.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.76: O King, remembering again and again this wondrous and holy dialogue between Keśava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.41.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.41: O Parantapa, the duties of Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras are distributed according to the guṇas born of their own nature (svabhāva).

Bhagavad Gītā 18.42.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.42: Equanimity of mind (śama), self-restraint (dama), austerity (tapas), purity (śauca), patience (kṣānti), uprightness (ārjava), knowledge (jñāna), experiential wisdom (vijñāna), and faith in the Supreme (āstikya) — these are the natural duties of a Brāhmaṇa.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.77.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.77: And remembering again and again that most marvellous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King, and I rejoice again and again.

Bhagavad Gītā 18.78.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.78: Wherever there is Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Yoga, and wherever there is Pārtha, the archer, there are certain to be fortune, victory, prosperity, and unswerving righteousness. This is my conviction.
